objects.name: Device.
objects.desc: The top-level object for a Device.

objects.name: Device.Services.
objects.desc: This object contains general services information.

objects.name: Device.DeviceInfo.
objects.desc: This object contains general device information.

objects.name: Device.DeviceInfo.VendorConfigFile.{i}.
objects.desc: Every instance of this object is a Vendor Configuration File, and contains parameters associated with the Vendor Configuration File. This table of Vendor Configuration Files is for information only and does not allow the Controller to operate on these files in any way. Whenever the Agent successfully restores a configuration file as a result of the Restore() Command, the Agent MUST update this Object. At most one entry in this table can exist with a given value for Alias , or with a given val...

objects.name: Device.DeviceInfo.MemoryStatus.
objects.desc: Status of the device's physical memory.

objects.name: Device.DeviceInfo.MemoryStatus.MemoryMonitor.
objects.desc: This object specifies information that the device has obtained via sampling the memory utilization (RAM) on the device.

objects.name: Device.DeviceInfo.ProcessStatus.
objects.desc: Status of the processes on the device.

objects.name: Device.DeviceInfo.ProcessStatus.CPU.{i}.
objects.desc: This object describes the utilization metrics for each CPU on the device. It also defines the monitoring actions that are automatically triggered when specific utilization thresholds are crossed. At most one entry in this table can exist with a given value for Name , or with a given value for Alias .

objects.name: Device.DeviceInfo.ProcessStatus.Process.{i}.
objects.desc: List of all processes running on the device. At most one entry in this table can exist with a given value for PID .

objects.name: Device.DeviceInfo.PowerStatus.
objects.desc: Status of the power consumption of the device.

objects.name: Device.DeviceInfo.PowerStatus.PowerSensor.{i}.
objects.desc: Represents the power sensor parameters including voltage, current, and power measurements. At most one entry in this table can exist with a given value for Name , or with a given value for Alias .

objects.name: Device.DeviceInfo.TemperatureStatus.
objects.desc: Status of the temperature of the device.

objects.name: Device.DeviceInfo.TemperatureStatus.TemperatureSensor.{i}.
objects.desc: This object represents information that the device has obtained via sampling an internal temperature sensor. At most one entry in this table can exist with a given value for Name , or with a given value for Alias .

objects.name: Device.DeviceInfo.NetworkProperties.
objects.desc: This object defines the parameters that describe how the device handles network traffic.

objects.name: Device.DeviceInfo.LogRotate.{i}.
objects.desc: This Object details the available rotation settings for vendor log file rotation. Based on [ A YANG Data Model for Syslog Configuration/YANGSYSLOG ]. At most one entry in this table can exist with a given value for Alias , or with a given value for Name . On creation of a new table entry, the Agent MUST (if not supplied by the Controller on creation) choose initial values for Alias and Name such that the new entry does not conflict with any existing entries.

objects.name: Device.DeviceInfo.LogRotate.{i}.LogFile.{i}.
objects.desc: Each table entry represents a Log File. This table of log files is informational only and does not allow the Controller to operate on these files in any way. At most one entry in this table can exist with a given value for Alias , or with a given value for Name .

objects.name: Device.DeviceInfo.VendorLogFile.{i}.
objects.desc: Each table entry represents a Vendor Log File. This table of log files is informational only and does not allow the Controller to operate on these files in any way. At most one entry in this table can exist with a given value for Alias , or with a given value for Name .

objects.name: Device.DeviceInfo.Location.{i}.
objects.desc: This object contains Location information. At most one entry in this table can exist with the same values for both Source and ExternalSource . On creation of a new table entry, the Agent MUST (if not supplied by the Controller on creation) choose an initial value for ExternalSource such that the new entry does not conflict with any existing entries.

objects.name: Device.DeviceInfo.DeviceImageFile.{i}.
objects.desc: This object describes an image of the device. At most one entry in this table can exist with a given value for Location , or with a given value for Alias .

objects.name: Device.DeviceInfo.FirmwareImage.{i}.
objects.desc: Top-level object for mapping firmware images. This is a static table – the number of object instances in this table is defined by the firmware that is currently running. At most one entry in this table can exist with a given value for Alias .

objects.name: Device.DeviceInfo.KernelFaults.
objects.desc: A fault in the context of the Kernel refers to a situation where the kernel encounters a critical error or a bug that it cannot recover from. When this happens, the kernel generates a "fault message" or "kernel panic", which provides information about the error, the state of the system at the time of the error, and a stack trace of function calls leading up to the error.

objects.name: Device.DeviceInfo.KernelFaults.KernelFault.{i}.
objects.desc: Each table entry represents a Kernel fault that is stored on the device. At most one entry in this table can exist with a given value for Alias .

objects.name: Device.DeviceInfo.KernelFaults.Stats.{i}.
objects.desc: Each table entry represents statistics for a particular recorded Kernel Fault Type. At most one entry in this table can exist with a given value for Alias , or with a given value for Type .

objects.name: Device.DeviceInfo.ProcessFaults.
objects.desc: Monitoring process faults and configuring the operating system to generate crash dumps and core files is essential for diagnosing and troubleshooting issues with applications and processes.

objects.name: Device.DeviceInfo.ProcessFaults.ProcessFault.{i}.
objects.desc: Each table entry represents a process fault that is stored on the device. At most one entry in this table can exist with a given value for Alias .

objects.name: Device.DeviceInfo.ProcessFaults.Stats.{i}.
objects.desc: Each table entry represents statistics for a particular recorded Process Fault Type. At most one entry in this table can exist with a given value for Alias , or with a given value for Type .

objects.name: Device.DeviceInfo.Reboots.
objects.desc: The monitoring of reboot reasons is essential for diagnosing and troubleshooting issues with applications and processes running on the Device.

objects.name: Device.DeviceInfo.Reboots.Reboot.{i}.
objects.desc: Each table entry represents a reboot reason that is stored on the device. When the maximum Reboot entries as indicated by MaxRebootEntries are reached, the next boot entry overrides the object with the oldest TimeStamp . At most one entry in this table can exist with a given value for Alias , or with a given value for TimeStamp .

objects.name: Device.DeviceInfo.BootTiming.
objects.desc: Boot performance metrics for monitoring and analyzing device boot time and milestones. This object provides detailed historical timing metrics for the most recent boot cycle, allowing for performance analysis and troubleshooting of boot-related issues.

objects.name: Device.DeviceInfo.BootTiming.LastBootMilestone.{i}.
objects.desc: Each table entry represents a milestone reached during the boot process referenced by LastRebootRef . This table is cleared and repopulated on each new boot. At most one entry in this table can exist with a given value for Alias , or with a given value for BootStage .

objects.name: Device.Time.
objects.desc: This object contains global parameters relating to the NTP time clients and or servers that are active in the device. This object can be used to model SNTP and NTP clients and servers. Both NTP and SNTP have identical packet formats and use the same mathematical operations to calculate client time, clock offset, and roundtrip delay. From the perspective of an NTP or SNTP server, there is no difference between NTP and SNTP clients, and from the perspective of an NTP or SNTP client, there is no...

objects.name: Device.Time.Client.{i}.
objects.desc: This object contains parameters relating to an time client instance. At most one entry in this table can exist with a given value for Alias . On creation of a new table entry, the Agent MUST (if not supplied by the Controller on creation) choose an initial value for Alias such that the new entry does not conflict with any existing entries.

objects.name: Device.Time.Client.{i}.Authentication.
objects.desc: This object contains parameters relating to enabling security for the time client.

objects.name: Device.Time.Client.{i}.Stats.
objects.desc: This object specifies the statistic parameters for the time client. [ Chapter 8 NTP Yang Module/RFC9249 ]

objects.name: Device.Time.Server.{i}.
objects.desc: This object contains parameters relating to an time server instance. At most one entry in this table can exist with a given value for Alias . On creation of a new table entry, the Agent MUST (if not supplied by the Controller on creation) choose an initial value for Alias such that the new entry does not conflict with any existing entries.

objects.name: Device.Time.Server.{i}.Authentication.
objects.desc: This object contains parameters relating to enabling security for the NTP Server.

objects.name: Device.Time.Server.{i}.Stats.
objects.desc: This object specifies the statistic parameters for the NTP server. [ Chapter 8 NTP Yang Module/RFC9249 ]

objects.name: Device.UserInterface.
objects.desc: This object contains parameters relating to the user interface of the CPE.

objects.name: Device.UserInterface.HTTPAccess.{i}.
objects.desc: HTTPAccess is used for modeling the different web interfaces that may be either locally or remotely available in the device. For example with Software Modules it is possible to install multiple services that embed a web interface like a Video service or Photo service . An instance of the HTTPAccess can model a web interface that is embedded in the device firmware or installed through a Software Modules management system. Access to the web interface MAY require user authentication. To have acc...

objects.name: Device.UserInterface.HTTPAccess.{i}.Session.{i}.
objects.desc: Web server session list. Note: This parameter was demoted to readOnly in the Device:2.17 version. At most one entry in this table can exist with a given value for SessionID .

objects.name: Device.UserInterface.LocalDisplay.
objects.desc: This object describes how to remotely manage the initial positioning of a user interface on a device's local display.

objects.name: Device.UserInterface.Messages.
objects.desc: Definition of user information message displays.

objects.name: Device.SFPs.
objects.desc: This object describes the Small Form-Factor Pluggable (SFP) cages and the transceivers hosted in them. The object definition is based on parts of [ SFF-8024 ] and [ SFF-8472 ]. This data model is extensible to support new SFP management protocol standards in the future.

objects.name: Device.SFPs.SFPCage.{i}.
objects.desc: This object describes a cage into which an SFP is inserted. This object can also describe an instance of Small Form Factor (SFF) units soldered on to the platform. At most one entry in this table can exist with a given value for Alias , or with a given value for Name .

objects.name: Device.SFPs.Mgmt.
objects.desc: This object describes the elements of an SFP that are exposed through the given management interface.

objects.name: Device.SFPs.Mgmt.SFF8472.{i}.
objects.desc: This object describes an SFP in a cage or the SFF present that can be managed as per SFF-8472 standard. At most one entry in this table can exist with a given value for Alias , or with a given value for Name .

objects.name: Device.SFPs.Mgmt.SFF8472.{i}.Transceiver.
objects.desc: This object describes the Transceiver present in the SFP. The Transceiver object here models the electrical interface to the SFP from the host and the function that enables transmission and reception of electrical or optical signals over the link connected. The Transceiver object is agnostic of the underlying protocol used in the transmission.

objects.name: Device.SFPs.Mgmt.SFF8472.{i}.Transceiver.Thresholds.
objects.desc: Each alarm and warning quantity has a corresponding high alarm, low alarm, high warning and low warning threshold. These factory preset values allows the determination of when a particular value is outside of “normal” limits as determined by the transceiver manufacturer. It is assumed that these values will vary with different technologies and different implementations and are vendor specific. The values here represent the values after any required calibration. See [ Table 9-5/SFF-8472 ].

objects.name: Device.SFPs.Mgmt.SFF8472.{i}.Transceiver.Status.
objects.desc: This object contains real time diagnostic and control values and status fields. See [ Table 9-16/SFF-8472 ]. The CPE MUST reset the interface’s Stats parameters (unless otherwise stated in individual object or parameter descriptions) either when the interface becomes operationally down due to a previous administrative down (i.e. the interface’s Status parameter transitions to a down state after the interface is disabled) or when the interface becomes administratively up (i.e. the interface’s ...

objects.name: Device.SFPs.Mgmt.SFF8472.{i}.Transceiver.Alarms.
objects.desc: This object contains the state of the SFP internal Diagnostic Alarms Flags [ Table 9-17/SFF-8472 ].

objects.name: Device.SFPs.Mgmt.SFF8472.{i}.Transceiver.Warnings.
objects.desc: This object contains the state of the SFP internal Diagnostic Warning Flags [ Table 9-17/SFF-8472 ]. Warning flags indicate conditions outside the normally guaranteed bounds but not necessarily causes of immediate link failures. Certain warning flags may also be defined by the manufacturer as end-of-life indicators (such as for higher than expected bias currents in a constant power control loop). A flag is set for each warning that is active. Implementation is vendor specific. An SFP module h...

objects.name: Device.SFPs.SFPProperties.
objects.desc: Object to help implementations to determine the SFP type. See SFP for more info. In the future the object can be expanded to show other properties of SFPs, e.g., the polarity of certain pins.

objects.name: Device.SFPs.SFPProperties.SFP.{i}.
objects.desc: List of SFPs to help implementations to determine the SFP type. SFPCage.{i}.SFPType reports the SFP type. SFPs themselves do not report their type. Implementations typically try to determine a value for that parameter based on the values for parameters such as: Mgmt.SFF8472.{i}.Transceiver.Transceiver Mgmt.SFF8472.{i}.Transceiver.BRNominal Mgmt.SFF8472.{i}.Transceiver.Wavelength This approach is not foolproof: many SFPs do not report correct values. They e.g. might report 0 as value for all t...

objects.name: Device.SFPs.AllowedSFPs.
objects.desc: Object specifying which pluggable SFPs the CPE should block or allow. The object is not applicable for built-in modules/SFPs (the CPE should always allow built-in modules/SFPs). When blocking a PON SFP, i.e. an SFP of type "G-PON", "XG-PON", "NG-PON2" or "XGS-PON", it's expected that the ANI using the SFP does not reach O5, i.e. that XPON.ONU.{i}.ANI.{i}.TC.ONUActivation.ONUState will not become O5. When blocking a MoCA SFP, it's expected that the MoCA interface using the SFP does not become ...

objects.name: Device.SFPs.AllowedSFPs.AllowedSFP.{i}.
objects.desc: Table of entries to classify pluggable SFPs. The CPE should allow any pluggable SFP which matches at least one of the entries; the CPE should block any SFP which does not match any entries. Example 1: allow all optical Ethernet SFPs Add entry with SFPType set to "Optical Ethernet" and with all other classification criteria set to the empty string. Example 2: allow XGS-PON SFP with "VendorA" as vendor name and "PartA" as part number Add entry with following values: SFPType = "XGS-PON" VendorNa...

objects.name: Device.InterfaceStack.{i}.
objects.desc: This table contains information about the relationships between the multiple layers of interface objects ([ Section 4.3/TR-181i2 ]). In particular, it contains information on which interfaces run on top of which other interfaces. This table is auto-generated by the CPE based on the LowerLayers parameters on individual interface objects. Each table row represents a "link" between two interface objects, a higher-layer interface object (referenced by HigherLayer ) and a lower-layer interface obj...

objects.name: Device.DSL.
objects.desc: This object models DSL lines, DSL channels, DSL bonding, and DSL diagnostics. The specific interface objects defined here are Line , Channel , and BondingGroup . Each Line models a layer 1 DSL Line interface, and each Channel models a layer 1 DSL Channel interface where multiple channels can run over a DSL line. In the case where bonding is configured, it is expected that BondingGroup is stacked above the Channel instances within its group.

objects.name: Device.DSL.Line.{i}.
objects.desc: DSL Line table (a stackable interface object as described in [ Section 4.2/TR-181i2 ]). This table models physical DSL lines. At most one entry in this table can exist with a given value for Alias , or with a given value for Name .

objects.name: Device.DSL.Line.{i}.Stats.
objects.desc: Throughput statistics for this interface. The CPE MUST reset the interface's Stats parameters (unless otherwise stated in individual object or parameter descriptions) either when the interface becomes operationally down due to a previous administrative down (i.e. the interface's Status parameter transitions to a down state after the interface is disabled) or when the interface becomes administratively up (i.e. the interface's Enable parameter transitions from false to true ). Administrative a...

objects.name: Device.DSL.Line.{i}.Stats.Total.
objects.desc: This object contains DSL line total statistics. See [ Chapter 7.2.6/G.997.1 ]. Note: The Total parameters SHOULD NOT be reset when the interface statistics are reset via an interface disable / enable cycle.

objects.name: Device.DSL.Line.{i}.Stats.Showtime.
objects.desc: This object contains DSL line statistics accumulated since the most recent DSL Showtime. See [ Chapter 7.2.6/G.997.1 ]. Note: The Showtime parameters SHOULD NOT be reset when the interface statistics are reset via an interface disable / enable cycle.

objects.name: Device.DSL.Line.{i}.Stats.LastShowtime.
objects.desc: This object contains DSL line statistics accumulated since the second most recent DSL Showtime. See [ Chapter 7.2.6/G.997.1 ]. Note: The LastShowtime parameters SHOULD NOT be reset when the interface statistics are reset via an interface disable / enable cycle.

objects.name: Device.DSL.Line.{i}.Stats.CurrentDay.
objects.desc: This object contains DSL line statistics accumulated during the current day. See [ Chapter 7.2.6/G.997.1 ]. Note: The CurrentDay parameters SHOULD NOT be reset when the interface statistics are reset via an interface disable / enable cycle.

objects.name: Device.DSL.Line.{i}.Stats.QuarterHour.
objects.desc: This object contains DSL line statistics accumulated during the current quarter hour. See [ Chapter 7.2.6/G.997.1 ]. Note: The QuarterHour parameters SHOULD NOT be reset when the interface statistics are reset via an interface disable / enable cycle.

objects.name: Device.DSL.Line.{i}.TestParams.
objects.desc: This object contains the DSL line test parameters that are available during the L0 (i.e., Showtime) state.

objects.name: Device.DSL.Line.{i}.DataGathering.
objects.desc: This object models the DSL data gathering function at the VTU-R. This only applies to VDSL2. Note: see ITU-T Recommendation [ G.993.2 ].

objects.name: Device.DSL.Channel.{i}.
objects.desc: DSL Channel table (a stackable interface object as described in [ Section 4.2/TR-181i2 ]). This table models DSL channel(s) on top of physical DSL lines. At most one entry in this table can exist with a given value for Alias , or with a given value for Name .

objects.name: Device.DSL.Channel.{i}.Stats.
objects.desc: Throughput statistics for this interface. The CPE MUST reset the interface's Stats parameters (unless otherwise stated in individual object or parameter descriptions) either when the interface becomes operationally down due to a previous administrative down (i.e. the interface's Status parameter transitions to a down state after the interface is disabled) or when the interface becomes administratively up (i.e. the interface's Enable parameter transitions from false to true ). Administrative a...

objects.name: Device.DSL.Channel.{i}.Stats.Total.
objects.desc: This object contains DSL channel total statistics [ G.997.1 ]. Note: The Total parameters SHOULD NOT be reset when the interface statistics are reset via an interface disable / enable cycle.

objects.name: Device.DSL.Channel.{i}.Stats.Showtime.
objects.desc: This object contains DSL channel statistics accumulated since the most recent DSL Showtime [ G.997.1 ]. Note: The Showtime parameters SHOULD NOT be reset when the interface statistics are reset via an interface disable / enable cycle.

objects.name: Device.DSL.Channel.{i}.Stats.LastShowtime.
objects.desc: This object contains DSL channel statistics accumulated since the second most recent DSL Showtime [ G.997.1 ]. Note: The LastShowtime parameters SHOULD NOT be reset when the interface statistics are reset via an interface disable / enable cycle.

objects.name: Device.DSL.Channel.{i}.Stats.CurrentDay.
objects.desc: This object contains DSL channel statistics accumulated during the current day [ G.997.1 ]. Note: The CurrentDay parameters SHOULD NOT be reset when the interface statistics are reset via an interface disable / enable cycle.

objects.name: Device.DSL.Channel.{i}.Stats.QuarterHour.
objects.desc: This object contains DSL channel statistics accumulated during the current quarter hour [ G.997.1 ]. Note: The QuarterHour parameters SHOULD NOT be reset when the interface statistics are reset via an interface disable / enable cycle.

objects.name: Device.DSL.BondingGroup.{i}.
objects.desc: DSL bonding group table (a stackable interface object as described in [ Section 4.2/TR-181i2 ]). Each instance is a bonding group, and is expected to be stacked above a Channel instance or a FAST.Line instance for each bonded channel in the group. Many of the parameters within this object, including LowerLayers , are read-only because bonding is not expected to be configured by a Controller. The DSL bonding data model is closely aligned with [ TR-159 ]. Corresponds to [ TR-159 ] oBondingGroup...

objects.name: Device.DSL.BondingGroup.{i}.Stats.
objects.desc: Throughput statistics for this interface. The CPE MUST reset the interface's Stats parameters (unless otherwise stated in individual object or parameter descriptions) either when the interface becomes operationally down due to a previous administrative down (i.e. the interface's Status parameter transitions to a down state after the interface is disabled) or when the interface becomes administratively up (i.e. the interface's Enable parameter transitions from false to true ). Administrative a...

objects.name: Device.DSL.BondingGroup.{i}.Stats.Total.
objects.desc: Total statistics for this bonding group. Note: The Total parameters SHOULD NOT be reset when the interface statistics are reset via an interface disable / enable cycle.

objects.name: Device.DSL.BondingGroup.{i}.Stats.CurrentDay.
objects.desc: Current day statistics for this bonding group. Note: The CurrentDay parameters SHOULD NOT be reset when the interface statistics are reset via an interface disable / enable cycle.

objects.name: Device.DSL.BondingGroup.{i}.Stats.QuarterHour.
objects.desc: Current quarter hour statistics for this bonding group. Note: The QuarterHour parameters SHOULD NOT be reset when the interface statistics are reset via an interface disable / enable cycle.

objects.name: Device.DSL.BondingGroup.{i}.BondedChannel.{i}.
objects.desc: DSL bonded channel table. Each table entry represents a bonded channel within the bonding group, and is associated with exactly one Channel instance or one FAST.Line instance. There MUST be an instance of BondedChannel for each DSL channel or FAST line that is bonded. When a Channel or FAST.Line is no longer bonded, then the CPE MUST delete the corresponding BondedChannel instance. However, when a bonded Channel or FAST.Line becomes disabled, the channel remains bonded and so the correspondin...

objects.name: Device.DSL.BondingGroup.{i}.BondedChannel.{i}.Ethernet.
objects.desc: Per-channel [ G.998.2 ] Ethernet-based bonding parameters.

objects.name: Device.DSL.BondingGroup.{i}.BondedChannel.{i}.Ethernet.Stats.
objects.desc: Per-channel [ G.998.2 ] Ethernet-based bonding statistics. These relate to the [ G.998.2 ] PME (Physical Medium Entity) Aggregation Function (PAF) lower layer (per-channel) interfaces. The CPE MUST reset the Stats parameters either when the interface becomes operationally down due to a previous administrative down (i.e. the interface's Status parameter transitions to a down state after the interface is disabled) or when the interface becomes administratively up (i.e. the interface's Enable pa...

objects.name: Device.DSL.BondingGroup.{i}.Ethernet.
objects.desc: Ethernet-based bonding parameters [ G.998.2 ]. This object MUST be present if, and only if, BondScheme is Ethernet . This object is a member of a union, i.e., it is a member of a group of objects of which only one can exist at a given time.

objects.name: Device.DSL.BondingGroup.{i}.Ethernet.Stats.
objects.desc: [ G.998.2 ] Ethernet-based bonding statistics. These relate to the [ G.998.2 ] PME (Physical Medium Entity) Aggregation Function (PAF) and to its upper layer interface. PAF lower layer interface statistics are in the BondedChannel.{i}.Ethernet.Stats objects. The CPE MUST reset the Stats parameters either when the interface becomes operationally down due to a previous administrative down (i.e. the interface's Status parameter transitions to a down state after the interface is disabled) or when...

objects.name: Device.DSL.Diagnostics.
objects.desc: The DSL Diagnostics object.

objects.name: Device.FAST.
objects.desc: This object models FAST (defined in ITU Recommendation [ G.9701 ]) lines. Each Line models a layer 1 FAST Line interface.

objects.name: Device.FAST.Line.{i}.
objects.desc: FAST Line table (a stackable interface object as described in [ Section 4.2/TR-181i2 ]). This table models physical FAST lines. At most one entry in this table can exist with a given value for Alias , or with a given value for Name .

objects.name: Device.FAST.Line.{i}.Stats.
objects.desc: Throughput statistics for this interface. The CPE MUST reset the interface's Stats parameters (unless otherwise stated in individual object or parameter descriptions) either when the interface becomes operationally down due to a previous administrative down (i.e. the interface's Status parameter transitions to a down state after the interface is disabled) or when the interface becomes administratively up (i.e. the interface's Enable parameter transitions from false to true ). Administrative a...

objects.name: Device.FAST.Line.{i}.Stats.Total.
objects.desc: This object contains DSL line total statistics. Note: The Total parameters SHOULD NOT be reset when the interface statistics are reset via an interface disable / enable cycle.

objects.name: Device.FAST.Line.{i}.Stats.Showtime.
objects.desc: This object contains FAST line statistics since the most recent showtime. Note: The Total parameters SHOULD NOT be reset when the interface statistics are reset via an interface disable / enable cycle.

objects.name: Device.FAST.Line.{i}.Stats.LastShowtime.
objects.desc: This object contains FAST line statistics since the second most recent showtime. Note: The Total parameters SHOULD NOT be reset when the interface statistics are reset via an interface disable / enable cycle.

objects.name: Device.FAST.Line.{i}.Stats.CurrentDay.
objects.desc: This object contains FAST line statistics accumulated during the current day. Note: The Total parameters SHOULD NOT be reset when the interface statistics are reset via an interface disable / enable cycle.

objects.name: Device.FAST.Line.{i}.Stats.QuarterHour.
objects.desc: This object contains FAST line statistics accumulated during the current quarter hour. Note: The Total parameters SHOULD NOT be reset when the interface statistics are reset via an interface disable / enable cycle.

objects.name: Device.FAST.Line.{i}.TestParams.
objects.desc: This object contains the FAST line test parameters that are available during the L0 (i.e., Showtime) state.

objects.name: Device.Optical.
objects.desc: This object models a generic optical interface. It defines an Interface object that models a layer 1 optical interface that is capable of transporting Ethernet packets. For historical reasons, the data model definition is based on parts of [ G.988 ]. However, it is not intended to model anything specific to IEEE PON or ITU-T PON technologies. Note that this object is not intended to model the optical transceiver either.

objects.name: Device.Optical.Interface.{i}.
objects.desc: Optical interface table (a stackable interface object as described in [ Section 4.2/TR-181i2 ]). This table models physical optical interfaces. At most one entry in this table can exist with a given value for Alias , or with a given value for Name .

objects.name: Device.Optical.Interface.{i}.Stats.
objects.desc: Throughput statistics for this interface. The CPE MUST reset the interface's Stats parameters (unless otherwise stated in individual object or parameter descriptions) either when the interface becomes operationally down due to a previous administrative down (i.e. the interface's Status parameter transitions to a down state after the interface is disabled) or when the interface becomes administratively up (i.e. the interface's Enable parameter transitions from false to true ). Administrative a...

objects.name: Device.Cellular.
objects.desc: This object models cellular interfaces and access points.

objects.name: Device.Cellular.Interface.{i}.
objects.desc: Cellular interface table (a stackable interface object as described in [ Section 4.2/TR-181i2 ]). Each instance of this object models a cellular modem with a single radio and can reference multiple TrustedElements.SIM. . At most one entry in this table can exist with a given value for Alias , or with a given value for Name .

objects.name: Device.Cellular.Interface.{i}.Stats.
objects.desc: Throughput statistics for this interface. The CPE MUST reset the interface's Stats parameters (unless otherwise stated in individual object or parameter descriptions) either when the interface becomes operationally down due to a previous administrative down (i.e. the interface's Status parameter transitions to a down state after the interface is disabled) or when the interface becomes administratively up (i.e. the interface's Enable parameter transitions from false to true ). Administrative a...

objects.name: Device.Cellular.Interface.{i}.SMS.
objects.desc: The object models SMS (Short Message Service) features.

objects.name: Device.Cellular.Interface.{i}.SMS.Storage.{i}.
objects.desc: Represents a SMS storage location. Each instance of this object corresponds to a distinct SMS storage area. Multiple instances of this object may exist, each representing a different storage type (e.g., SM SIM card, ME device memory). At most one entry in this table can exist with a given value for Alias .

objects.name: Device.Cellular.Interface.{i}.SMS.Incoming.
objects.desc: This object models incoming SMS configuration.

objects.name: Device.Cellular.Interface.{i}.SMS.Outgoing.
objects.desc: This object models outgoing SMS configuration.

The CPE MUST reset the interface's Stats parameters (unless otherwise stated in individual object or parameter descriptions) either when the interface becomes operationally down due to a previous administrative down (i.e. the interface's Status parameter transitions to a down state after the interface is disabled) or when the interface becomes administratively up (i.e. the interface's Enable parameter transitions from false to true ). Administrative a...

objects.name: Device.UPA.Interface.{i}.AssociatedDevice.{i}.
objects.desc: This table contains information about PLC connections running between this UPA interface and other UPA devices. At most one entry in this table can exist with a given value for MACAddress .

objects.name: Device.UPA.Interface.{i}.ActiveNotch.{i}.
objects.desc: This object contains the list of active notches of the UPA interface. A UPA device can have notches in its spectrum, where no power is transmitted in a given part of the spectrum. These notches are typically located in amateur radio bands, to avoid interference. Note: All ActiveNotch entries can be enabled/disabled as a group using the ActiveNotchEnable parameter. At most one entry in this table can exist with a given value for Alias . On creation of a new table entry, the Agent MUST (if not ...

objects.name: Device.UPA.Interface.{i}.BridgeFor.{i}.
objects.desc: This object represents the bridge table of the UPA interface. Each instance is a bridge table entry. It shows the MAC addresses of the remote UPA devices with their associated port number, and the MAC addresses of the end-devices (PCs, STBs, routers, etc) connected to Ethernet port of the powerline adapters with their associated logical port. In this way the system identifies to which UPA device an external device is connected to. At most one entry in this table can exist with a given value f...

objects.name: Device.UPA.Diagnostics.
objects.desc: The UPA Diagnostics object.

objects.name: Device.WiFi.
objects.desc: The WiFi object is based on the IEEE 802.11 specifications ([ 802.11-2020 ]). It defines interface objects ( Radio and SSID ), and application objects ( AccessPoint and EndPoint ).

objects.name: Device.WiFi.DataElements.
objects.desc: This object represents the Wi-Fi Alliance Data Elements as defined in [ DataElements ] with extended capabilities in additional objects whose names begin with MultiAP.

objects.name: Device.WiFi.DataElements.Network.
objects.desc: This object describes a Wi-Fi network containing 1 or more Access Point (AP) devices.

objects.name: Device.WiFi.DataElements.Network.SSID.{i}.
objects.desc: This object specifies SSIDs for fronthaul use across all agents in this Wi-Fi Multi-AP network, or on this single-AP. Also specifies the Band for each SSID . The Alias can be used to uniquely refer to this table entry corresponding to a BSS even if the SSID were to change. Note that VLAN IDs (VIDs) can be configured per SSID with Device.{i}.SSIDtoVIDMapping.{i} . At most one entry in this table can exist with a given value for Alias .

objects.name: Device.WiFi.DataElements.Network.STABlock.{i}.
objects.desc: This object indicates stations (STAs) for which client association is blocked. optionally the BSSID(s) the STA is blocked from associating to. In multi-AP cases, this should be implemented by Wi-Fi EasyMesh [ EasyMesh ] client association control. Stations that are already associated shall be disassociated if STABlock.{i}.Schedule.{i}. indicates so. At most one entry in this table can exist with a given value for BlockedSTA . On creation of a new table entry, the Agent MUST (if not supplied b...

objects.name: Device.WiFi.DataElements.Network.STABlock.{i}.Schedule.{i}.
objects.desc: Each instance of this object provides a schedule where client association is blocked for BlockedSTA [ Section 11.6/EasyMesh ]. At most one entry in this table can exist with a given value for Alias . On creation of a new table entry, the Agent MUST (if not supplied by the Controller on creation) choose an initial value for Alias such that the new entry does not conflict with any existing entries.

objects.name: Device.WiFi.DataElements.Network.ProvisionedDPP.{i}.
objects.desc: This table contains provisioned Device Provisioning Protocol (DPP) Boostrap URIs [ Section 5.2.1/EasyConnect ] which contain bootstrapping keys available to the Multi-AP controller for trusted third party onboarding of new Multi-AP agents. At most one entry in this table can exist with a given value for Alias . On creation of a new table entry, the Agent MUST (if not supplied by the Controller on creation) choose an initial value for Alias such that the new entry does not conflict with any ex...

objects.name: Device.WiFi.DataElements.Network.MultiAPSteeringSummaryStats.
objects.desc: The summary of statistics related to Multi-AP Steering for the Wi-Fi network. The counters contained in MultiAPSteeringSummaryStats are all reset on reboot.

objects.name: Device.WiFi.DataElements.Network.Device.{i}.
objects.desc: Each instance of this object represents an individual EasyMesh Agent or single-AP device in the Wi-Fi network. This table MUST contain at least 1 entry. At most one entry in this table can exist with a given value for ID .

objects.name: Device.WiFi.DataElements.Network.Device.{i}.Default8021Q.{i}.
objects.desc: The default 802.1Q settings for EasyMesh service prioritization [ EasyMesh ]. At most one entry in this table can exist with a given value for PrimaryVID . On creation of a new table entry, the Agent MUST (if not supplied by the Controller on creation) choose an initial value for PrimaryVID such that the new entry does not conflict with any existing entries.

objects.name: Device.WiFi.DataElements.Network.Device.{i}.SSIDtoVIDMapping.{i}.
objects.desc: The Service Set Identifier (SSID) to VLAN ID mapping for EasyMesh traffic separation [ EasyMesh ]. At most one entry in this table can exist with a given value for SSID .

objects.name: Device.WiFi.DataElements.Network.Device.{i}.CACStatus.{i}.
objects.desc: Latest Channel Availability Check (CAC) Status Report from the device. At most one entry in this table can exist with a given value for TimeStamp .

objects.name: Device.WiFi.DataElements.Network.Device.{i}.CACStatus.{i}.CACAvailableChannel.{i}.
objects.desc: This object describes available channels identified by Channel Availability Check (CAC). At most one entry in this table can exist with the same values for both OpClass and Channel .

objects.name: Device.WiFi.DataElements.Network.Device.{i}.CACStatus.{i}.CACNonOccupancyChannel.{i}.
objects.desc: This object describes channels identified by Channel Availability Check (CAC) that may not be occupied. At most one entry in this table can exist with the same values for both OpClass and Channel .

objects.name: Device.WiFi.DataElements.Network.Device.{i}.CACStatus.{i}.CACActiveChannel.{i}.
objects.desc: This object describes channels with ongoing Channel Availability Check (CAC). At most one entry in this table can exist with the same values for both OpClass and Channel .

objects.name: Device.WiFi.DataElements.Network.Device.{i}.SPRule.{i}.
objects.desc: This object describes a list of service prioritization (SP) rules [ EasyMesh ]. At most one entry in this table can exist with a given value for ID .

objects.name: Device.WiFi.DataElements.Network.Device.{i}.IEEE1905Security.{i}.
objects.desc: This object describes the IEEE 1905 security capabilities. At most one entry in this table can exist with a given value for OnboardingProtocol .

objects.name: Device.WiFi.DataElements.Network.Device.{i}.AnticipatedChannels.{i}.
objects.desc: This object contains a table of Wi-Fi 6 [ 802.11ax ] operating classes, and channels within those operating classes, which have anticipated channel preference. Operating Class contains an enumerated value from [ Table E-4/802.11ax ]. At most one entry in this table can exist with a given value for OpClass .

objects.name: Device.WiFi.DataElements.Network.Device.{i}.AnticipatedChannelUsage.{i}.
objects.desc: This object reports Wi-Fi 6 [ 802.11ax ] anticipated medium usage on channels (and subsets of those channels) on which the device is operating. At most one entry in this table can exist with a given value for OpClass .

objects.name: Device.WiFi.DataElements.Network.Device.{i}.AnticipatedChannelUsage.{i}.Entry.{i}.
objects.desc: This object reports an entry for anticipated channel usage [ 802.11ax ]. At most one entry in this table can exist with a given value for BurstStartTime .

objects.name: Device.WiFi.DataElements.Network.Device.{i}.BackhaulDown.{i}.
objects.desc: This object identifies EasyMesh Agents and their interfaces that are downstream of this EasyMesh Agent and have backhaul to this EasyMesh Agent. At most one entry in this table can exist with a given value for BackhaulDownALID .

objects.name: Device.WiFi.DataElements.Network.Device.{i}.AFCAvailableSpectrum.
objects.desc: This object contains the Available Spectrum Inquiry request and response message defined by [ Section 8.2.5/EasyMesh ]. This provides information of 6 GHz spectrum availability as determined by an Automated Frequency Coordination (AFC) system [ AFCSDI ].

objects.name: Device.WiFi.DataElements.Network.Device.{i}.MultiAPDevice.
objects.desc: This object represents an individual Access Point device.

objects.name: Device.WiFi.DataElements.Network.Device.{i}.MultiAPDevice.Backhaul.
objects.desc: This object represents an individual Access Point device's Backhaul and unique aspects in the Wi-Fi network. The endpoints of the backhaul interface are represented by the (Device's ID and interface MAC Address). This object represents the upward view of the backhaul interface. The two endpoints of the backhaul interface are - ( BackhaulDeviceID , BackhaulMACAddress ) of the uplinked Backhaul Device - MACAddress of this Access Point Device. An empty string is reserved for the Backhaul instanc...

objects.name: Device.WiFi.DataElements.Network.Device.{i}.MultiAPDevice.Backhaul.CurrentOperatingClassProfile.{i}.
objects.desc: Describes one of the current Operating Classes in use by this Radio. One Opeating Class is indicated for each current Operating Channel Bandwidth. The Channel indicated for the 20 MHz Operating Class is equal to the current primary channel. At most one entry in this table can exist with a given value for Class .

objects.name: Device.WiFi.DataElements.Network.Device.{i}.MultiAPDevice.Backhaul.Stats.
objects.desc: This object represents the statistics of the backhaul interface view from the current Device's ID

objects.name: Device.WiFi.DataElements.Network.Device.{i}.Radio.{i}.
objects.desc: This object represents all of the individual Radios contained within the identified Access Point device known to the controller. This table MUST contain at least 1 entry. At most one entry in this table can exist with a given value for ID .

objects.name: Device.WiFi.DataElements.Network.Device.{i}.Radio.{i}.ScanResult.{i}.
objects.desc: The list of neighboring Access Points discovered by a Radio organized per Operating Class and Channel tuple.

objects.name: Device.WiFi.DataElements.Network.Device.{i}.Radio.{i}.ScanResult.{i}.OpClassScan.{i}.
objects.desc: The Operating Class of neighboring Access Points discovered by a Radio during a channel scan. At most one entry in this table can exist with a given value for OperatingClass .

objects.name: Device.WiFi.DataElements.Network.Device.{i}.Radio.{i}.ScanResult.{i}.OpClassScan.{i}.ChannelScan.{i}.
objects.desc: The Channel associated with an Operating Class of neighboring Access Points discovered by a Radio during a channel scan. At most one entry in this table can exist with a given value for Channel .

objects.name: Device.WiFi.DataElements.Network.Device.{i}.Radio.{i}.ScanResult.{i}.OpClassScan.{i}.ChannelScan.{i}.NeighborBSS.{i}.
objects.desc: The neighboring BSS discovered by a Radio during a channel scan. For MLDs, MLDMACAddress identifies the AP MLD for which this NeighborBSS.{i}. is an affilated AP, other affiliated APs in this NeighborBSS have the same value of MLDMACAddress . At most one entry in this table can exist with a given value for BSSID .

objects.name: Device.WiFi.DataElements.Network.Device.{i}.Radio.{i}.BackhaulSta.
objects.desc: Contains the Medium Access Control (MAC) address of the STA on this radio providing Wi-Fi backhaul to this device.

objects.name: Device.WiFi.DataElements.Network.Device.{i}.Radio.{i}.ScanCapability.
objects.desc: This object describes the channel scan capabilities of a radio.

objects.name: Device.WiFi.DataElements.Network.Device.{i}.Radio.{i}.ScanCapability.OpClassChannels.{i}.
objects.desc: Table of the operating classes (selected from [ Table E-4/802.11ax ]) and channel numbers in each operating class that the radio is capable of scanning. This table MUST contain at least 1 entry. At most one entry in this table can exist with a given value for OpClass .

objects.name: Device.WiFi.DataElements.Network.Device.{i}.Radio.{i}.CACCapability.
objects.desc: This object describes the Channel Availability Check (CAC) capabilities of a radio.

objects.name: Device.WiFi.DataElements.Network.Device.{i}.Radio.{i}.CACCapability.CACMethod.{i}.
objects.desc: List of Channel Availability Check (CAC) method information for each type of CAC that the radio can perform. Each type is defined by a method and time to complete. For each type, the classes and channels allowed are enumerated. This table MUST contain at least 0 and at most 4 entries. At most one entry in this table can exist with a given value for Method .

objects.name: Device.WiFi.DataElements.Network.Device.{i}.Radio.{i}.CACCapability.CACMethod.{i}.OpClassChannels.{i}.
objects.desc: Table of the operating classes (selected from [ Table E-4/802.11ax ]) and channel numbers in each operating class supported for this method of CAC. This table MUST contain at least 1 entry. At most one entry in this table can exist with a given value for OpClass .

objects.name: Device.WiFi.DataElements.Network.Device.{i}.Radio.{i}.Capabilities.
objects.desc: This object represents the capabilities of the radio which may be different from the current operational configuration.

objects.name: Device.WiFi.DataElements.Network.Device.{i}.Radio.{i}.Capabilities.WiFi6APRole.
objects.desc: Describes the Wi-Fi 6 capabilities for the AP role.

objects.name: Device.WiFi.DataElements.Network.Device.{i}.Radio.{i}.Capabilities.WiFi6bSTARole.
objects.desc: Describes the Wi-Fi 6 capabilities for the backhaul Station (bSTA) role.

objects.name: Device.WiFi.DataElements.Network.Device.{i}.Radio.{i}.Capabilities.WiFi7APRole.
objects.desc: This object describes the Wi-Fi 7 capabilities for the AP role including Multi-Link Operation (MLO) capabilities. [ EasyMesh ] Source: Wi-Fi 7 Agent Capabilities TLV.

objects.name: Device.WiFi.DataElements.Network.Device.{i}.Radio.{i}.Capabilities.WiFi7APRole.EMLMRFreqSeparation.{i}.
objects.desc: This object describes the required frequency separation from the specified radio RUID for MLO Enhanced Multi-Link Multi-Radio (EMLMR) operation. [ EasyMesh ] Source: Wi-Fi 7 Agent Capabilities TLV. At most one entry in this table can exist with a given value for RUID .

objects.name: Device.WiFi.DataElements.Network.Device.{i}.Radio.{i}.Capabilities.WiFi7APRole.EMLSRFreqSeparation.{i}.
objects.desc: This object describes the required frequency separation from the specified radio RUID for MLO Enhanced Multi-Link Single-Radio (EMLSR) operation. [ EasyMesh ] Source: Wi-Fi 7 Agent Capabilities TLV. At most one entry in this table can exist with a given value for RUID .

objects.name: Device.WiFi.DataElements.Network.Device.{i}.Radio.{i}.Capabilities.WiFi7APRole.STRFreqSeparation.{i}.
objects.desc: This object describes the required frequency separation from the specified radio RUID for MLO Simultaneous Transmit and Receive (STR) operation. [ EasyMesh ] Source: Wi-Fi 7 Agent Capabilities TLV. At most one entry in this table can exist with a given value for RUID .

objects.name: Device.WiFi.DataElements.Network.Device.{i}.Radio.{i}.Capabilities.WiFi7APRole.NSTRFreqSeparation.{i}.
objects.desc: This object describes the required frequency separation from the specified radio RUID for MLO Non-Simultaneous Transmit and Receive (NSTR) operation. [ EasyMesh ] Source: Wi-Fi 7 Agent Capabilities TLV. At most one entry in this table can exist with a given value for RUID .

objects.name: Device.WiFi.DataElements.Network.Device.{i}.Radio.{i}.Capabilities.WiFi7bSTARole.
objects.desc: This object describes the Wi-Fi 7 capabilities for the backhaul Station (bSTA) role including Multi-Link Operation (MLO) capabilities. [ EasyMesh ] Source: Wi-Fi 7 Agent Capabilities TLV.

objects.name: Device.WiFi.DataElements.Network.Device.{i}.Radio.{i}.Capabilities.WiFi7bSTARole.EMLMRFreqSeparation.{i}.
objects.desc: This object describes the required frequency separation from the specified radio RUID for MLO Enhanced Multi-Link Multi-Radio (EMLMR) operation. [ EasyMesh ] Source: Wi-Fi 7 Agent Capabilities TLV. At most one entry in this table can exist with a given value for RUID .

objects.name: Device.WiFi.DataElements.Network.Device.{i}.Radio.{i}.Capabilities.WiFi7bSTARole.EMLSRFreqSeparation.{i}.
objects.desc: This object describes the required frequency separation from the specified radio RUID for MLO Enhanced Multi-Link Single-Radio (EMLSR) operation. [ EasyMesh ] Source: Wi-Fi 7 Agent Capabilities TLV. At most one entry in this table can exist with a given value for RUID .

objects.name: Device.WiFi.DataElements.Network.Device.{i}.Radio.{i}.Capabilities.WiFi7bSTARole.STRFreqSeparation.{i}.
objects.desc: This object describes the required frequency separation from the specified radio RUID for MLO Simultaneous Transmit and Receive (STR) operation. [ EasyMesh ] Source: Wi-Fi 7 Agent Capabilities TLV. At most one entry in this table can exist with a given value for RUID .

objects.name: Device.WiFi.DataElements.Network.Device.{i}.Radio.{i}.Capabilities.WiFi7bSTARole.NSTRFreqSeparation.{i}.
objects.desc: This object describes the required frequency separation from the specified radio RUID for MLO Non-Simultaneous Transmit and Receive (NSTR) operation. [ EasyMesh ] Source: Wi-Fi 7 Agent Capabilities TLV. At most one entry in this table can exist with a given value for RUID .

objects.name: Device.WiFi.DataElements.Network.Device.{i}.Radio.{i}.Capabilities.AKMFrontHaul.{i}.
objects.desc: Authentication and Key Management (AKM) Suite (security mode) capabilities for the fronthaul BSS. At most one entry in this table can exist with a given value for OUI .

objects.name: Device.WiFi.DataElements.Network.Device.{i}.Radio.{i}.Capabilities.AKMBackhaul.{i}.
objects.desc: Authentication and Key Management (AKM) Suite (security mode) capabilities for the backhaul BSS. At most one entry in this table can exist with a given value for OUI .

objects.name: Device.WiFi.DataElements.Network.Device.{i}.Radio.{i}.Capabilities.CapableOperatingClassProfile.{i}.
objects.desc: Describes one of the possible Operating Classes supported by this Radio. At most one entry in this table can exist with a given value for Class .

objects.name: Device.WiFi.DataElements.Network.Device.{i}.Radio.{i}.Capabilities.HaLowCapabilities.
objects.desc: This object describes the capabilities of the Wi-Fi HaLow radio, most of which can be extracted from the Sub 1 GHz (S1G) capabilities Information Element (IE) in [ Section 9.4.2.200.2/802.11-2020 ].

objects.name: Device.WiFi.DataElements.Network.Device.{i}.Radio.{i}.CurrentOperatingClassProfile.{i}.
objects.desc: Describes one of the current Operating Classes in use by this Radio. One Operating Class is indicated for each current Operating Channel Bandwidth. The Channel indicated for the 20 MHz Operating Class is equal to the current primary channel. At most one entry in this table can exist with a given value for Class .

objects.name: Device.WiFi.DataElements.Network.Device.{i}.Radio.{i}.DisAllowedOpClassChannels.{i}.
objects.desc: The operating classes, and list of channels for each operating class, which are not allowed to be used on this radio. At most one entry in this table can exist with a given value for OpClass . On creation of a new table entry, the Agent MUST (if not supplied by the Controller on creation) choose an initial value for OpClass such that the new entry does not conflict with any existing entries.

objects.name: Device.WiFi.DataElements.Network.Device.{i}.Radio.{i}.OpClassPreference.{i}.
objects.desc: Values represent Channel Preference TLV values in the most recent Channel Preference Report message [ Section 17.2.13/EasyMesh ]. Each entry in this table describes one of the operating classes for which Channel Preference has been reported. A Preference score of 15 must be inferred for all channel/operating classes not present in this table, unless that channel/operating class has been reported as statically non-operable in the most recent AP Radio Basic Capabilities TLV [ Section 17.2.7/Eas...

objects.name: Device.WiFi.DataElements.Network.Device.{i}.Radio.{i}.SpatialReuse.
objects.desc: The spatial reuse configuration of this radio. Applies only to Wi-Fi 6 [ 802.11ax ] and possibly later generations of radios. Acronyms: Spatial Reuse Group (SRG), Overlapping Basic Service Set (OBSS), Preamble Detection (PD).

objects.name: Device.WiFi.DataElements.Network.Device.{i}.Radio.{i}.BSS.{i}.
objects.desc: A single logical BSS operating on this radio. This table MUST contain at least 1 entry. At most one entry in this table can exist with a given value for BSSID .

objects.name: Device.WiFi.DataElements.Network.Device.{i}.Radio.{i}.BSS.{i}.QMDescriptor.{i}.
objects.desc: This object contains a table of DescriptorElement . At most one entry in this table can exist with a given value for ClientMAC .

objects.name: Device.WiFi.DataElements.Network.Device.{i}.Radio.{i}.BSS.{i}.MUConfig.
objects.desc: This object provides Multiuser (MU)-specific BSS configuration.

objects.name: Device.WiFi.DataElements.Network.Device.{i}.Radio.{i}.BSS.{i}.MUStats.
objects.desc: This object provides packet statistics for a Multiuser (MU) BSS.

objects.name: Device.WiFi.DataElements.Network.Device.{i}.Radio.{i}.BSS.{i}.MultiAPSteering.
objects.desc: A single logical Access Point operating on this radio.

objects.name: Device.WiFi.DataElements.Network.Device.{i}.Radio.{i}.BSS.{i}.ThroughputTestResult.
objects.desc: Object containing the results of the most recent throughput (speed) test from the BSS to a station (STA).

objects.name: Device.WiFi.DataElements.Network.Device.{i}.Radio.{i}.BSS.{i}.LatencyTestResult.
objects.desc: Object containing the results of the most recent latency test set from the BSS to a station (STA). Each latency test set includes a number of individual echo tests. Each echo test result provides a sample of round-trip times and statistics on all the echo tests in this latency test are reported in this object.

objects.name: Device.WiFi.DataElements.Network.Device.{i}.Radio.{i}.BSS.{i}.SetQoSManagementInput.
objects.desc: This object records inputs for setting QoS Management [ Section 20/EasyMesh ].

objects.name: Device.WiFi.DataElements.Network.Device.{i}.Radio.{i}.BSS.{i}.STA.{i}.
objects.desc: Object describing a single Associated Device (STA). The Backhaul STAs (bSTAs) with which other Device.WiFi.DataElements.Network.Device.{i}. connect to this BSS are included in this table. STA MLD and bSTA MLD are not included, and are instead part of Device.WiFi.DataElements.Network.Device.{i}.APMLD.{i}.STAMLD.{i}. . AffiliatedSTAs and AffiliatedbSTAs are not included, and are instead part of Device.WiFi.DataElements.Network.Device.{i}.APMLD.{i}.STAMLD.{i}.AffiliatedSTA.{i}. . This table MUST...

objects.name: Device.WiFi.DataElements.Network.Device.{i}.Radio.{i}.BSS.{i}.STA.{i}.MultiAPSTA.
objects.desc: The summary of statistics and operations for an individual STA on the Wi-Fi network. The counters contained in MultiAPSTA are all reset on reboot.

objects.name: Device.WiFi.DataElements.Network.Device.{i}.Radio.{i}.BSS.{i}.STA.{i}.MultiAPSTA.SteeringSummaryStats.
objects.desc: The summary of statistics related to Multi-AP Steering for this STA on the Wi-Fi network. The counters contained in SteeringSummaryStats are all reset on reboot.

objects.name: Device.WiFi.DataElements.Network.Device.{i}.Radio.{i}.BSS.{i}.STA.{i}.MultiAPSTA.SteeringHistory.{i}.
objects.desc: The history of Multi-AP Steering for this STA on the Wi-Fi network. The contents of this multi-instance object are reset on reboot. At most one entry in this table can exist with the same values for all of Time , APOrigin and APDestination .

objects.name: Device.WiFi.DataElements.Network.Device.{i}.Radio.{i}.BSS.{i}.STA.{i}.WiFi6Capabilities.
objects.desc: Describes the Wi-Fi 6 capabilities of the Associated Device (STA).

objects.name: Device.WiFi.DataElements.Network.Device.{i}.Radio.{i}.BSS.{i}.STA.{i}.HaLowCapabilities.
objects.desc: Describes the HaLow capabilities of the Associated Device (STA). most of which can be extracted from the Sub 1 GHz (S1G) capabilities Information Element (IE) in [ Section 9.4.2.200.2/802.11-2020 ].

objects.name: Device.WiFi.DataElements.Network.Device.{i}.Radio.{i}.BSS.{i}.STA.{i}.TIDQueueSizes.{i}.
objects.desc: Object describing Traffic Identifiers (TIDs), and Queue Size for each TID, for this Associated Device (STA). At most one entry in this table can exist with a given value for TID .

objects.name: Device.WiFi.DataElements.Network.Device.{i}.Radio.{i}.MultiAPRadio.
objects.desc: This object represents an individual Access Point Radio in the Wi-Fi network.

objects.name: Device.WiFi.DataElements.Network.Device.{i}.Radio.{i}.UnassociatedSTA.{i}.
objects.desc: Each instance represents a station (STA) that has been discovered by the Radio but is not associated to any of the BSS operating on the Radio. At most one entry in this table can exist with a given value for MACAddress .

objects.name: Device.WiFi.DataElements.Network.Device.{i}.WPS.
objects.desc: This object contains Wi-Fi Protected Setup (WPS) Push Button Configuration (PBC) configuration and status as specified in [ WPSv1.0 ] or [ WPS 2.0 ]). In EasyMesh [ EasyMesh ] this object applies to fronthaul only.

objects.name: Device.WiFi.DataElements.Network.Device.{i}.APMLD.{i}.
objects.desc: Table of Multi-Link Operation (MLO) capable Access Points (APs) on this EasyMesh Agent or Single AP device. [ EasyMesh ] source: Agent AP MLD Configuration TLV. At most one entry in this table can exist with a given value for MLDMACAddress .

objects.name: Device.WiFi.DataElements.Network.Device.{i}.APMLD.{i}.APMLDConfig.
objects.desc: This object describes the Wi-Fi 7 Multi-Link Operation (MLO) configuration of the Multi-Link Device (MLD) Access Point (AP), [ EasyMesh ] source: Agent AP MLD Configuration TLV.

objects.name: Device.WiFi.DataElements.Network.Device.{i}.APMLD.{i}.APMLDConfig.TIDToOpClassPolicy.{i}.
objects.desc: Table of Traffic Identifier (TID) to Operating Class to be used as a policy when configuring TID-to-Link Mapping in the Multi-Link Operation (MLO) capable access point (AP). Each table entry describes the mapping between a particular TID and direction and the required current Operating Class for any link to be used for this TID when constructing a TID-to-Link Map [ Section 20.2.8/EasyMesh ]. At most one entry in this table can exist with the same values for both TID and Direction . On creatio...

objects.name: Device.WiFi.DataElements.Network.Device.{i}.APMLD.{i}.TIDLinkMap.{i}.
objects.desc: Table of Traffic Identifier (TID) to Link Mappings of the Multi-Link Operation (MLO) capable access point (AP). Each table entry describes the mapping between a particular TID and direction and preferred link. [ EasyMesh ] source: TID-to-Link Mapping Policy TLV. At most one entry in this table can exist with a given value for TID .

objects.name: Device.WiFi.DataElements.Network.Device.{i}.APMLD.{i}.LinkToOpClassMap.{i}.
objects.desc: This object describes the relationship between an Affiliated AP and the Operating Class (OpClass) of the Radio that the Affiliated AP is operating on [ Section 20.2.8/EasyMesh ]. At most one entry in this table can exist with a given value for LinkID .

objects.name: Device.WiFi.DataElements.Network.Device.{i}.APMLD.{i}.AffiliatedAP.{i}.
objects.desc: The Access Points (APs) affiliated to the AP MLD. [ EasyMesh ] Source: Agent AP MLD Configuration TLV. Counters in this object only include MLD traffic. At most one entry in this table can exist with a given value for BSSID .

objects.name: Device.WiFi.DataElements.Network.Device.{i}.APMLD.{i}.STAMLD.{i}.
objects.desc: This object describes Multi-Link Operation (MLO) capable stations (STAs), also known as client Multilink Devices (MLDs), associated to this MLO capable Access Point. [ EasyMesh ] source: Associated Clients TLV. At most one entry in this table can exist with a given value for MLDMACAddress .

objects.name: Device.WiFi.DataElements.Network.Device.{i}.APMLD.{i}.STAMLD.{i}.WiFi7Capabilities.
objects.desc: This object describes the Wi-Fi 7 capabilities for this STA MLD including Multi-Link Operation (MLO) capabilities. [ EasyMesh ] Source: Wi-Fi 7 Agent Capabilities TLV.

objects.name: Device.WiFi.DataElements.Network.Device.{i}.APMLD.{i}.STAMLD.{i}.STAMLDConfig.
objects.desc: This object describes the Wi-Fi 7 Multi-Link Operation (MLO) configuration of the Multi-Link Device (MLD) station (STA, also called associated device). Note this may differ from the WiFi7 capabilities of the device. [ EasyMesh ] source: Associated STA MLD Configuration Report TLV.

objects.name: Device.WiFi.DataElements.Network.Device.{i}.APMLD.{i}.STAMLD.{i}.STATIDLinkMap.{i}.
objects.desc: Table of Traffic Identifier (TID) to Link Mappings of the Multi-Link Operation (MLO) capable station (STA). Each table entry describes the mapping between a particular TID and direction and preferred link. [ EasyMesh ] source: TID-to-Link Mapping Policy TLV. At most one entry in this table can exist with a given value for TID .

objects.name: Device.WiFi.DataElements.Network.Device.{i}.APMLD.{i}.STAMLD.{i}.AffiliatedSTA.{i}.
objects.desc: This object describes stations (STAs, also called associated devices) that are affiliated to this Multi-Link Device (MLD) STA. [ EasyMesh ] source: Associated STA MLD Configuration TLV. At most one entry in this table can exist with a given value for MACAddress .

objects.name: Device.WiFi.DataElements.Network.Device.{i}.bSTAMLD.
objects.desc: This object represents the Multi-Link Operation (MLO) capable backhaul station (bSTA) operating on this EasyMesh Agent. Only one MLO capable bSTA per EasyMesh Agent is allowed. [ EasyMesh ] source: Backhaul STA MLD Configuration TLV.

objects.name: Device.WiFi.DataElements.Network.Device.{i}.bSTAMLD.bSTAMLDConfig.
objects.desc: This object describes the Multi-Link Operation (MLO) configuration of a Multi-Link Device (MLD) backhaul STA (bSTA). [ EasyMesh ] source: Backhaul STA MLD Configuration TLV.

objects.name: Device.WiFi.DataElements.Network.PreferredBackhauls.{i}.
objects.desc: This object specifies the preferred backhaul links as populated by SetPreferredBackhauls() . At most one entry in this table can exist with a given value for bSTAMACAddress .

objects.name: Device.WiFi.DataElements.AssociationEvent.
objects.desc: This object contains the events generated when a STA associates to a BSS.

objects.name: Device.WiFi.DataElements.DisassociationEvent.
objects.desc: This object contains the events generated when an Associated Device (STA) disassociates from a BSS.

objects.name: Device.WiFi.DataElements.FailedConnectionEvent.
objects.desc: This object contains the events generated when a Station (STA) fails to connect to a Basic Service Set (BSS).

objects.name: Device.WiFi.Templates.
objects.desc: Wi-Fi Configuration Templates provide a comprehensive way to configure Wi-Fi. Configuration Templates can be applied across multiple deployments in an operator's network, and across multiple APs, radios and BSSs. A set of Configuration Templates can be pre-defined, which can then handle many different services and scenarios by matching flags to select a particular template depending on AP or radio capabilities and topology. Different BSSs can be configured across different radios to provision...

objects.name: Device.WiFi.Templates.Network.
objects.desc: This Network either has the Configuration Template Manager (CTM) deploy BSS(s) according to the templates, or has all BSS(s) be disabled.

objects.name: Device.WiFi.Templates.BSSTemplate.{i}.
objects.desc: Table of Basic Service Set (BSS) templates for Wi-Fi configuration. At most one entry in this table can exist with a given value for BSSTemplateID , or with a given value for Alias . On creation of a new table entry, the Agent MUST (if not supplied by the Controller on creation) choose initial values for BSSTemplateID and Alias such that the new entry does not conflict with any existing entries.

objects.name: Device.WiFi.Templates.RadioTemplate.{i}.
objects.desc: Table of RadioTemplates for Wi-Fi configuration. At most one entry in this table can exist with a given value for RadioTemplateID , or with a given value for Alias . On creation of a new table entry, the Agent MUST (if not supplied by the Controller on creation) choose initial values for RadioTemplateID and Alias such that the new entry does not conflict with any existing entries.

objects.name: Device.WiFi.Templates.SecurityTemplate.{i}.
objects.desc: Table of SecurityTemplates for Wi-Fi configuration [ WPA3 ]. At most one entry in this table can exist with a given value for SecurityTemplateID , or with a given value for Alias . On creation of a new table entry, the Agent MUST (if not supplied by the Controller on creation) choose initial values for SecurityTemplateID and Alias such that the new entry does not conflict with any existing entries.

objects.name: Device.WiFi.Templates.SecurityTemplate.{i}.RSNE.
objects.desc: This object describes the Robust Security Network Element (RSNE). This object is only used by the Configuration Template Manager if the SecurityIEs is empty.

objects.name: Device.WiFi.Templates.SecurityTemplate.{i}.RSNOE.
objects.desc: This object describes the RSNOE element. This object is only used by the Configuration Template Manager if the SecurityIEs is empty.

objects.name: Device.WiFi.Templates.SecurityTemplate.{i}.RSNO2E.
objects.desc: This object describes the RSNO2E element. This object is only used by the Configuration Template Manager if the SecurityIEs is empty.

objects.name: Device.WiFi.Templates.SecurityTemplate.{i}.RSNXE.
objects.desc: This object indicates the value the BSS transmits in the RSNXE element. This object is only used by the Configuration Template Manager if the SecurityIEs is empty.

objects.name: Device.WiFi.Templates.SecurityTemplate.{i}.RSNXOE.
objects.desc: This object indicates the value the BSS transmits in the RSNXOE element. This object is only used by the Configuration Template Manager if the SecurityIEs is empty.

objects.name: Device.WiFi.Templates.SecurityGroup.{i}.
objects.desc: Table of SecurityGroups for Wi-Fi configuration [ WPA3 ]. At most one entry in this table can exist with a given value for SecurityGroupID . On creation of a new table entry, the Agent MUST (if not supplied by the Controller on creation) choose an initial value for SecurityGroupID such that the new entry does not conflict with any existing entries.

objects.name: Device.WiFi.Templates.APMLDTemplate.{i}.
objects.desc: Table of AP Multi-Link Device (MLD) templates (APMLDTemplate) for Wi-Fi configuration [ Section 17.2.96, Agent AP MLD Configuration TLV/EasyMesh ]. At most one entry in this table can exist with a given value for APMLDTemplateID , or with a given value for Alias . On creation of a new table entry, the Agent MUST (if not supplied by the Controller on creation) choose initial values for APMLDTemplateID and Alias such that the new entry does not conflict with any existing entries.

objects.name: Device.WiFi.Templates.SSCTemplate.{i}.
objects.desc: Table of Service Set Collection (SSC) templates (SSCTemplate) for Wi-Fi configuration. At most one entry in this table can exist with a given value for SSCTemplateID , or with a given value for Alias . On creation of a new table entry, the Agent MUST (if not supplied by the Controller on creation) choose initial values for SSCTemplateID and Alias such that the new entry does not conflict with any existing entries.

objects.name: Device.WiFi.AFC.
objects.desc: Object that contains all the information regarding Automated Frequency Coordination (AFC) configuration and status for 6 GHz operation. The object definition is based on specification [ AFCSDI ], which defines the AFC system for communicating to the AFC server.

objects.name: Device.WiFi.AFC.DeviceDescriptor.
objects.desc: This object contains the information of an AP or Fixed Client Device used by the AFC system.

objects.name: Device.WiFi.AFC.Location.
objects.desc: Object that contains references to the location of the AP or Fixed Client Device obtained from GPS, Barometer, External or Manual sources.

objects.name: Device.WiFi.AFC.Stats.
objects.desc: Object that contains information about AFC requests and responses.

objects.name: Device.WiFi.Radio.{i}.

If the device can establish more than one connection simultaneously (e.g. a dual radio device), a separate Radio instance MUST be used for each physical radio of the device. objects.name: Device.WiFi.Radio.{i}.Capabilities.
objects.desc: This object represents the capabilities of the radio which may be different from the current operational configuration.

objects.name: Device.WiFi.Radio.{i}.Capabilities.WiFi7APRole.
objects.desc: This object describes the Wi-Fi 7 capabilities for the AP role. [ EasyMesh ] Source: Wi-Fi 7 Agent Capabilities TLV.

objects.name: Device.WiFi.Radio.{i}.Capabilities.WiFi7APRole.EMLMRFreqSeparation.{i}.
objects.desc: This object describes the required frequency separation from the specified radio RUID for MLO Enhanced Multi-Link Multi-Radio (EMLMR) operation. [ EasyMesh ] Source: Wi-Fi 7 Agent Capabilities TLV. At most one entry in this table can exist with a given value for RUID .

objects.name: Device.WiFi.Radio.{i}.Capabilities.WiFi7APRole.EMLSRFreqSeparation.{i}.
objects.desc: This object describes the required frequency separation from the specified radio RUID for MLO Enhanced Multi-Link Single-Radio (EMLSR) operation. [ EasyMesh ] Source: Wi-Fi 7 Agent Capabilities TLV. At most one entry in this table can exist with a given value for RUID .

objects.name: Device.WiFi.Radio.{i}.Capabilities.WiFi7APRole.STRFreqSeparation.{i}.
objects.desc: This object describes the required frequency separation from the specified radio RUID for MLO Simultaneous Transmit and Receive (STR) operation. [ EasyMesh ] Source: Wi-Fi 7 Agent Capabilities TLV. At most one entry in this table can exist with a given value for RUID .

objects.name: Device.WiFi.Radio.{i}.Capabilities.WiFi7APRole.NSTRFreqSeparation.{i}.
objects.desc: This object describes the required frequency separation from the specified radio RUID for MLO Non-Simultaneous Transmit and Receive (NSTR) operation. [ EasyMesh ] Source: Wi-Fi 7 Agent Capabilities TLV. At most one entry in this table can exist with a given value for RUID .

objects.name: Device.WiFi.Radio.{i}.Capabilities.WiFi7STARole.
objects.desc: This object describes the Wi-Fi 7 capabilities for the backhaul Station (bSTA) role. [ EasyMesh ] Source: Wi-Fi 7 Agent Capabilities TLV.

objects.name: Device.WiFi.Radio.{i}.Capabilities.WiFi7STARole.EMLMRFreqSeparation.{i}.
objects.desc: This object describes the required frequency separation from the specified radio RUID for MLO Enhanced Multi-Link Multi-Radio (EMLMR) operation. [ EasyMesh ] Source: Wi-Fi 7 Agent Capabilities TLV. At most one entry in this table can exist with a given value for RUID .

objects.name: Device.WiFi.Radio.{i}.Capabilities.WiFi7STARole.EMLSRFreqSeparation.{i}.
objects.desc: This object describes the required frequency separation from the specified radio RUID for MLO Enhanced Multi-Link Single-Radio (EMLSR) operation. [ EasyMesh ] Source: Wi-Fi 7 Agent Capabilities TLV. At most one entry in this table can exist with a given value for RUID .

objects.name: Device.WiFi.Radio.{i}.Capabilities.WiFi7STARole.STRFreqSeparation.{i}.
objects.desc: This object describes the required frequency separation from the specified radio RUID for MLO Simultaneous Transmit and Receive (STR) operation. [ EasyMesh ] Source: Wi-Fi 7 Agent Capabilities TLV. At most one entry in this table can exist with a given value for RUID .

objects.name: Device.WiFi.Radio.{i}.Capabilities.WiFi7STARole.NSTRFreqSeparation.{i}.
objects.desc: This object describes the required frequency separation from the specified radio RUID for MLO Non-Simultaneous Transmit and Receive (NSTR) operation. [ EasyMesh ] Source: Wi-Fi 7 Agent Capabilities TLV. At most one entry in this table can exist with a given value for RUID .

objects.desc: WiFi SSID table (a stackable interface object as described in [ Section 4.2/TR-181i2 ]), where table entries model the MAC layer. At most one entry in this table can exist with a given value for Alias , or with a given value for Name , or with a given value for BSSID . objects.name: Device.WiFi.AccessPoint.{i}.
objects.desc: This object models an 802.11 connection from the perspective of a wireless access point. Each AccessPoint entry is associated with a particular SSID interface instance via the SSIDReference parameter. For enabled table entries, if SSIDReference is not a valid reference then the table entry is inoperable and the CPE MUST set Status to Error_Misconfigured . objects.name: Device.WiFi.AccessPoint.{i}.Security.
objects.desc: This object contains security related parameters that apply to a CPE acting as an Access Point [ 802.11-2007 ].

objects.name: Device.WiFi.AccessPoint.{i}.Interworking.
objects.desc: This object contains the settings to the interworking element as described in [ Section 9.4.2.91/802.11-2020 ].

objects.name: Device.WiFi.AccessPoint.{i}.ANQP.
objects.desc: This object contains the settings required for configuring the Access Network Query Protocol Information Elements as described in [ Section 9.4.5/802.11-2020 ].

objects.name: Device.WiFi.AccessPoint.{i}.Passpoint.
objects.desc: This object describes Passpoint/HotSpot 2.0 elements as defined in [ Passpoint ].

objects.name: Device.WiFi.AccessPoint.{i}.Passpoint.OSU.
objects.desc: This object implements Passpoint Online Sign Up as described in [ Section 4.3/Passpoint ].

objects.name: Device.WiFi.AccessPoint.{i}.WPS.
objects.desc: This object contains parameters related to Wi-Fi Protected Setup for this access point (as specified in [ WPSv1.0 ] or [ WPS 2.0 ]).

objects.name: Device.WiFi.AccessPoint.{i}.AssociatedDevice.{i}.
objects.desc: A table of the devices currently associated with the access point. At most one entry in this table can exist with a given value for MACAddress .

objects.name: Device.WiFi.AccessPoint.{i}.AssociatedDevice.{i}.Stats.
objects.desc: These count bytes or packets sent to, or received from, this Associated Device, which is a WiFi station associated to this access point. Packet counters here count 802.11 WiFi frames. The CPE MUST reset these Stats parameters (unless otherwise stated in individual object or parameter descriptions) either when the Status of the parent AccessPoint object transitions from Disabled to Enabled , or when it transitions from Enabled to Disabled .

objects.name: Device.WiFi.AccessPoint.{i}.AC.{i}.
objects.desc: This object contains parameters related to WiFi QoS for different 802.11e access categories (priorities). Access categories are: BE, BK, VI, and VO. These parameters can help control and monitor 802.11e Enhanced distributed channel access (EDCA). objects.name: Device.WiFi.AccessPoint.{i}.Accounting.
objects.desc: This object contains the parameters related to RADIUS accounting functionality for the access point.

Each EndPoint entry is associated with a particular SSID interface instance via the SSIDReference parameter, and an associated active Profile instance via the ProfileReference parameter. objects.name: Device.WiFi.EndPoint.{i}.Stats.
objects.desc: Throughput statistics for this end point.

objects.name: Device.WiFi.EndPoint.{i}.Security.
objects.desc: This object contains security related parameters that apply to a WiFi end point [ 802.11-2007 ].

objects.name: Device.WiFi.EndPoint.{i}.Profile.{i}.
objects.desc: EndPoint Profile table. At most one entry in this table can exist with a given value for Alias , or with the same values for all of SSID , Location and Priority . objects.name: Device.WiFi.EndPoint.{i}.Profile.{i}.Security.
objects.desc: This object contains security related parameters that apply to a WiFi End Point profile [ 802.11-2007 ].

objects.name: Device.WiFi.EndPoint.{i}.WPS.
objects.desc: This object contains parameters related to Wi-Fi Protected Setup [ WPSv1.0 ] for this end point.

objects.name: Device.Thread.
objects.desc: The Thread object is based on the Thread Group specifications: Thread 1.3.0 Specification [ ThreadSpec ]. It defines interface object ( Radio and MLE ), and application object ( BorderRouter ).

objects.name: Device.Thread.BorderRouter.{i}.
objects.desc: The BorderRouter is capable of forwarding between a Thread Network and a non-Thread Network. Each BorderRouter entry is associated with a particular Thread Network (or MLE) instance via the MLEReference parameter. At most one entry in this table can exist with a given value for Alias , or with a given value for BorderAgentID .

objects.name: Device.Thread.Radio.{i}.
objects.desc: This object models an 802.15.4 wireless radio ([ 802.15.4-2020 ]) on the device (a stackable interface object as described in [ Section 4.2/TR-181i2 ]). At most one entry in this table can exist with a given value for Alias , or with a given value for Name .

At most one entry in this table can exist with a given value for Alias , or with a given value for Name . objects.name: Device.Thread.MLE.{i}.Dataset.{i}.SecurityPolicy.
objects.desc: The SecurityPolicy provide an administrator a way to enable or disable certain security related behaviors.

objects.name: Device.Thread.MLE.{i}.AssociatedNode.{i}.Neighbor.{i}.
objects.desc: Entries in this table reference nodes that are immediate neighbors of the associated node instance. This table is empty if the RoutingRole is not a Router or Leader . At most one entry in this table can exist with a given value for NodeReference .

objects.name: Device.Thread.MLE.{i}.AssociatedNode.{i}.IPv6Address.{i}.

objects.name: Device.Thread.Node.{i}.
