commands.name: IPPing()
commands.desc: [ASYNC] This command provides access to an IP-layer ping test.

input.name: Interface
input.desc: The value MUST be the Path Name of a table row. The layer 2 or layer 3 interface over which the test is to be performed. Example: Device.IP.Interface.1 , Device.Bridge.1.Port.2 If the value is an empty string, the CPE MUST use its routing policy (IP Forwarding table entries), if necessary, to determine the appropriate interface.

input.name: ProtocolVersion
input.desc: [MANDATORY] Indicates the IP protocol to be used. Enumeration of: Any (Use either IPv4 or IPv6 depending on the system preference) IPv4 (Use IPv4 for the Ping requests) IPv6 (Use IPv6 for the Ping requests)

input.name: Host
input.desc: [MANDATORY] Host name or address of the host to ping. In the case where Host is specified by name, and the name resolves to more than one address, it is up to the device implementation to choose which address to use.

input.name: NumberOfRepetitions
input.desc: [MANDATORY] Number of repetitions of the ping test to perform before reporting the results.

input.name: Timeout
input.desc: [MANDATORY] Timeout in milliseconds for the ping test.

input.name: DataBlockSize
input.desc: [MANDATORY] Size of the data block in bytes to be sent for each ping.

input.name: DSCP
input.desc: DiffServ codepoint to be used for the test packets. By default the CPE SHOULD set this value to zero.

output.name: ⇐ Status
output.desc: Indicates the availability of diagnostics data. Enumeration of: Canceled (OPTIONAL) Complete Error (OPTIONAL) Error_CannotResolveHostName Error_NoRouteToHost (The CPE can not reach the requested Ping host address) Error_Internal Error_Other If the value of this parameter is anything other than Complete , the values of the other results parameters for this test are indeterminate.

output.name: ⇐ IPAddressUsed
output.desc: [ IPAddress ] Indicates which IP address was used to send the Ping request.

output.name: ⇐ SuccessCount
output.desc: Result parameter indicating the number of successful pings (those in which a successful response was received prior to the timeout) in the most recent ping test.

output.name: ⇐ FailureCount
output.desc: Result parameter indicating the number of failed pings in the most recent ping test.

output.name: ⇐ AverageResponseTime
output.desc: Result parameter indicating the average response time in milliseconds over all repetitions with successful responses of the most recent ping test. If there were no successful responses, this value MUST be zero.

output.name: ⇐ MinimumResponseTime
output.desc: Result parameter indicating the minimum response time in milliseconds over all repetitions with successful responses of the most recent ping test. If there were no successful responses, this value MUST be zero.

output.name: ⇐ MaximumResponseTime
output.desc: Result parameter indicating the maximum response time in milliseconds over all repetitions with successful responses of the most recent ping test. If there were no successful responses, this value MUST be zero.

output.name: ⇐ AverageResponseTimeDetailed
output.desc: Result parameter indicating the average response time in microseconds over all repetitions with successful responses of the most recent ping test. If there were no successful responses, this value MUST be zero.

output.name: ⇐ MinimumResponseTimeDetailed
output.desc: Result parameter indicating the minimum response time in microseconds over all repetitions with successful responses of the most recent ping test. If there were no successful responses, this value MUST be zero.

output.name: ⇐ MaximumResponseTimeDetailed
output.desc: Result parameter indicating the maximum response time in microseconds over all repetitions with successful responses of the most recent ping test. If there were no successful responses, this value MUST be zero.

commands.name: TraceRoute()
commands.desc: [ASYNC] This command defines access to an IP-layer trace-route test for the specified IP interface.

input.name: Interface
input.desc: The value MUST be the Path Name of a table row. The layer 2 or layer 3 interface over which the test is to be performed. Example: Device.IP.Interface.1 , Device.Bridge.1.Port.2 If the value is an empty string, the CPE MUST use its routing policy (IP Forwarding table entries), if necessary, to determine the appropriate interface.

input.name: ProtocolVersion
input.desc: [MANDATORY] Indicates the IP protocol to be used. Enumeration of: Any (Use either IPv4 or IPv6 depending on the system preference) IPv4 (Use IPv4 for the TraceRoute) IPv6 (Use IPv6 for the TraceRoute)

input.name: Host
input.desc: [MANDATORY] Host name or address of the host to find a route to. In the case where Host is specified by name, and the name resolves to more than one address, it is up to the device implementation to choose which address to use.

input.name: NumberOfTries
input.desc: Number of tries per hop. Set prior to running Diagnostic. By default, the CPE SHOULD set this value to 3.

input.name: Timeout
input.desc: Timeout in milliseconds for each hop of the trace route test. By default the CPE SHOULD set this value to 5000.

input.name: DataBlockSize
input.desc: Size of the data block in bytes to be sent for each trace route. By default, the CPE SHOULD set this value to 38.

input.name: DSCP
input.desc: DiffServ codepoint to be used for the test packets. By default the CPE SHOULD set this value to 0.

input.name: MaxHopCount
input.desc: The maximum number of hop used in outgoing probe packets (max TTL). By default the CPE SHOULD set this value to 30.

output.name: ⇐ Status
output.desc: Indicates the availability of diagnostics data. Enumeration of: Canceled (OPTIONAL) Complete Error (OPTIONAL) Error_CannotResolveHostName Error_NoRouteToHost (The CPE can not reach the requested TraceRoute host address) Error_MaxHopCountExceeded Error_Internal Error_Other If the value of this parameter is anything other than Complete , the values of the other results parameters for this test are indeterminate.

output.name: ⇐ IPAddressUsed
output.desc: [ IPAddress ] Indicates which IP address was used for TraceRoute.

output.name: ⇐ ResponseTime
output.desc: Result parameter indicating the response time in milliseconds the most recent trace route test. If a route could not be determined, this value MUST be zero.

output.name: ⇐ RouteHops.{i}.
output.desc: Contains the array of hop results returned. If a route could not be determined, this array will be empty This table's Instance Numbers MUST be 1, 2, 3... (assigned sequentially without gaps).

output.name: ⇐ Host
output.desc: Result parameter indicating the Host Name if DNS is able to resolve or IP Address of a hop along the discovered route.

output.name: ⇐ HostAddress
output.desc: If this parameter is not an empty string it will contain the last IP address of the host returned for this hop and the Host will contain the Host Name returned from the reverse DNS query.

output.name: ⇐ ErrorCode
output.desc: Contains the error code returned for this hop. This code is directly from the ICMP CODE field.

output.name: ⇐ RTTimes
output.desc: Comma-separated list (1 to 3 items) of unsigned integers. Each list item contains one or more round trip times in milliseconds (one for each repetition) for this hop. A list item of 0 indicates that the corresponding response was not received. Round trip times of less than 1 milliseconds MUST be rounded up to 1. The number of list entries is determined by the value of NumberOfTries .

commands.name: DownloadDiagnostics()
commands.desc: [ASYNC] This command defines the diagnostics configuration for a HTTP and FTP DownloadDiagnostics Test. Files received in the DownloadDiagnostics do not require file storage on the CPE device.

input.name: Interface
input.desc: The value MUST be the Path Name of a table row. The IP-layer interface over which the test is to be performed. Example: Device.IP.Interface.1 If the value is an empty string, the CPE MUST use its routing policy (IP Forwarding table entries), if necessary, to determine the appropriate interface.

input.name: DownloadURL
input.desc: [MANDATORY] The [ URL ] for the CPE to perform the download on. This parameter MUST be in the form of a valid HTTP [ RFC2616 ] or FTP [ RFC959 ] URL. When using FTP transport, FTP binary transfer MUST be used. When using HTTP transport, persistent connections MUST be used and pipelining MUST NOT be used. When using HTTP transport the HTTP Authentication MUST NOT be used. Note: For time based tests ( TimeBasedTestDuration > 0) the Controller MAY add a hint to duration of the test to the URL. S...

input.name: DSCP
input.desc: The DiffServ code point for marking packets transmitted in the test. The default value SHOULD be zero.

input.name: EthernetPriority
input.desc: Ethernet priority code for marking packets transmitted in the test (if applicable). The default value SHOULD be zero.

input.name: TimeBasedTestDuration
input.desc: Controls time based testing [ Section 4.3/TR-143 ]. When TimeBasedTestDuration > 0, TimeBasedTestDuration is the duration in seconds of a time based test. If TimeBasedTestDuration is 0, the test is not based on time, but on the size of the file to be downloaded. The default value SHOULD be 0.

input.name: TimeBasedTestMeasurementInterval
input.desc: The measurement interval duration in seconds for objects in IncrementalResult for a time based FTP/HTTP download test (when TimeBasedTestDuration > 0). The default value SHOULD be 0, which implies IncrementalResult collection is disabled. For example if TimeBasedTestDuration is 90 seconds and TimeBasedTestMeasurementInterval is 10 seconds , there will be 9 results in IncrementalResult , each with a 10 seconds duration.

input.name: TimeBasedTestMeasurementOffset
input.desc: This TimeBasedTestMeasurementOffset works in conjunction with TimeBasedTestMeasurementInterval to allow the interval measurement to start a number of seconds after BOMTime . The test measurement interval in IncrementalResult starts at time BOMTime + TimeBasedTestMeasurementOffset to allow for slow start window removal of file transfers. This TimeBasedTestMeasurementOffset is in seconds . The default value SHOULD be 0.

input.name: ProtocolVersion
input.desc: Indicates the IP protocol version to be used. The default value SHOULD be Any . Enumeration of: Any (Use either IPv4 or IPv6 depending on the system preference) IPv4 (Use IPv4 for the requests) IPv6 (Use IPv6 for the requests)

input.name: NumberOfConnections
input.desc: The number of connections to be used in the test. The default value SHOULD be 1. NumberOfConnections MUST NOT be set to a value greater than DownloadDiagnosticMaxConnections .

input.name: EnablePerConnectionResults
input.desc: The results must be returned in the PerConnectionResult table for every connection when set to true . The default value SHOULD be false .

output.name: ⇐ Status
output.desc: Indicates the availability of diagnostics data. Enumeration of: Complete Error_CannotResolveHostName Error_NoRouteToHost Error_InitConnectionFailed Error_NoResponse Error_TransferFailed Error_PasswordRequestFailed Error_LoginFailed Error_NoTransferMode Error_NoPASV Error_IncorrectSize Error_Timeout Error_Internal Error_Other If the value of this parameter is anything other than Complete , the values of the other results parameters for this test are indeterminate.

output.name: ⇐ IPAddressUsed
output.desc: [ IPAddress ] Indicates which IP address was used to send the request.

output.name: ⇐ ROMTime
output.desc: Request time in UTC, which MUST be specified to microsecond precision. For example: 2008-04-09T15:01:05.123456Z For HTTP this is the time at which the client sends the GET command. For FTP this is the time at which the client sends the RTRV command. If multiple connections are used, then ROMTime is set to the earliest ROMTime across all connections.

output.name: ⇐ BOMTime
output.desc: Begin of transmission time in UTC, which MUST be specified to microsecond precision For example: 2008-04-09T15:01:05.123456Z For HTTP this is the time at which the first data packet is received. For FTP this is the time at which the client receives the first data packet on the data connection. If multiple connections are used, then BOMTime is set to the earliest BOMTime across all connections.

output.name: ⇐ EOMTime
output.desc: End of transmission in UTC, which MUST be specified to microsecond precision. For example: 2008-04-09T15:01:05.123456Z For HTTP this is the time at which the last data packet is received. For FTP this is the time at which the client receives the last packet on the data connection. If multiple connections are used, then EOMTime is set to the latest EOMTime across all connections.

output.name: ⇐ TestBytesReceived
output.desc: [ StatsCounter64 ] The number of bytes received during the FTP/HTTP transaction including FTP/HTTP headers, between BOMTime and EOMTime across all connections.

output.name: ⇐ TotalBytesReceived
output.desc: [ StatsCounter64 ] The total number of bytes (at the IP layer) received on the Interface between BOMTime and EOMTime . This MAY be calculated by sampling Stats.BytesReceived on the Interface object at BOMTime and at EOMTime and subtracting. If Interface is an empty string, this parameter cannot be determined and SHOULD be 0.

output.name: ⇐ TotalBytesSent
output.desc: [ StatsCounter64 ] The total number of bytes (at the IP layer) sent on the Interface between BOMTime and EOMTime . If Interface is an empty string, this parameter cannot be determined and SHOULD be 0.

output.name: ⇐ TotalBytesReceived
output.desc: [ StatsCounter64 ] The total number of bytes (at the IP layer) received on the Interface between BOMTime and EOMTime . This MAY be calculated by sampling Stats.BytesReceived on the Interface object at BOMTime and at EOMTime and subtracting.

input.desc: The size of the file bytes to be uploaded to the server. The CPE MUST insure the appropriate number of bytes are sent.

commands.name: UDPEchoDiagnostics()
commands.desc: [ASYNC] This command defines the diagnostics configuration for a UDP Echo test [ Appendix A.1/TR-143 ] defined in [ RFC862 ] or a UDP Echo Plus test defined in [ Appendix A.1/TR-143 ].

input.name: Interface
input.desc: The value MUST be the Path Name of a row in the IP.Interface. table, or the Path Name of an interface layered above such a row, e.g., a row in the Logical.Interface. table. The IP-layer interface over which the test is to be performed. Example: Device.IP.Interface.1 If the value is an empty string, the CPE MUST use its routing policy (IP Forwarding table entries), if necessary, to determine the appropriate interface.

input.name: Host
input.desc: [MANDATORY] Host name or address of the host to perform tests to.

input.name: Port
input.desc: [MANDATORY] Port on the host to perform tests to. The default value MUST be 7 .

input.name: NumberOfRepetitions
input.desc: Number of repetitions of the test to perform before reporting the results. The default value SHOULD be 1.

input.name: Timeout
input.desc: [MANDATORY] Timeout in milliseconds for the test. That is, the amount of time to wait for the return of a packet that was sent to the Host .

input.name: DataBlockSize
input.desc: Size of the data block in bytes to be sent for each packet. The default value SHOULD be 24.

input.name: DSCP
input.desc: DiffServ codepoint to be used for the test packets. The default value SHOULD be zero.

input.name: InterTransmissionTime
input.desc: The time in milliseconds between the NumberOfRepetitions of packets sent during a given test. The default value SHOULD be 1000.

input.name: ProtocolVersion
input.desc: Indicates the IP protocol version to be used. The default value SHOULD be Any . Enumeration of: Any (Use either IPv4 or IPv6 depending on the system preference) IPv4 (Use IPv4 for the requests) IPv6 (Use IPv6 for the requests)

input.name: EnableIndividualPacketResults
input.desc: The results must be returned in the IndividualPacketResult table for every repetition of the test when set to true . The default value SHOULD be false .

output.name: ⇐ Status
output.desc: Indicates the availability of diagnostics data. Enumeration of: Complete Error_CannotResolveHostName Error_Internal Error_Other If the value of this parameter is anything other than Complete , the values of the other results parameters for this test are indeterminate.

output.name: ⇐ IPAddressUsed
output.desc: [ IPAddress ] Indicates which IP address was used to send the request.

output.name: ⇐ SuccessCount
output.desc: Result parameter indicating the number of successful packets (those in which a successful response was received prior to the timeout) in the most recent test.

output.name: ⇐ FailureCount
output.desc: Result parameter indicating the number of failed packets (those in which a successful response was not received prior to the timeout) in the most recent test.

output.name: ⇐ AverageResponseTime
output.desc: Result parameter indicating the average response time in microseconds over all repetitions with successful responses of the most recent test. If there were no successful responses, this value MUST be zero.

output.name: ⇐ MinimumResponseTime
output.desc: Result parameter indicating the minimum response time in microseconds over all repetitions with successful responses of the most recent test. If there were no successful responses, this value MUST be zero.

output.name: ⇐ MaximumResponseTime
output.desc: Result parameter indicating the maximum response time in microseconds over all repetitions with successful responses of the most recent test. If there were no successful responses, this value MUST be zero.

output.name: ⇐ IndividualPacketResult.{i}.
output.desc: This object provides the results from individual UDPEchoPlus test packets collected during a test if EnableIndividualPacketResults is set to true. It should contain NumberOfRepetitions objects. Instance numbers MUST start at 1 and sequentially increment as new instances are created. The instance number should match the TestIterationNumber field of the request and response packet. This table's Instance Numbers MUST be 1, 2, 3... (assigned sequentially without gaps).

output.name: ⇐ PacketSuccess
output.desc: Indicates that the response to this UDP Echo Plus packet sent was received by the client. When this value is true , then all the remaining parameters in this instance are valid. Otherwise only the values originally set by the CPE client (e.g. PacketSendTime and TestGenSN ) MAY be set to valid values.

output.name: ⇐ PacketSendTime
output.desc: Time the client sent this UDP Echo Plus packet in UTC, which MUST be specified to microsecond precision. For example: 2008-04-09T15:01:05.123456Z

output.name: ⇐ PacketReceiveTime
output.desc: Time the client receives the response packet in UTC, which MUST be specified to microsecond precision. For example: 2008-04-09T15:01:05.123456Z If this response is never received, PacketReceiveTime SHOULD be set to the Unknown Time value as specified in [ Section 3.2.2/TR-106 ].

output.name: ⇐ TestGenSN
output.desc: The TestGenSN field in the UDPEcho Plus packet [ Section A.1.4/TR-143 ] sent by the CPE client.

output.name: ⇐ TestRespSN
output.desc: The TestRespSN field in the response packet [ Section A.1.4/TR-143 ] from the UDP Echo Plus server (i.e. Host ) for this Echo Plus packet sent by the CPE client. If PacketSuccess is false , TestRespSN SHOULD be 0.

output.name: ⇐ TestRespRcvTimeStamp
output.desc: The TestRespRcvTimeStamp field in the response packet [ Section A.1.4/TR-143 ] from the UDP Echo Plus server (i.e. Host ) to record the reception time in microseconds of this UDP Echo Plus packet sent from the CPE client. If PacketSuccess is false , TestRespRcvTimeStamp SHOULD be 0.

output.name: ⇐ TestRespReplyTimeStamp
output.desc: The TestRespReplyTimeStamp field in the response packet [ Section A.1.4/TR-143 ] from the UDP Echo Plus server (i.e. Host ) to record the server reply time in microseconds of this UDP Echo Plus packet sent from the CPE client. That is, the time that the server returned the UDP Echo Plus packet. If PacketSuccess is false , TestRespReplyTimeStamp SHOULD be 0.

output.name: ⇐ TestRespReplyFailureCount
output.desc: The count value that was set by the UDP Echo Plus server (i.e. Host ) to record the number of dropped echo response packets by the server. This count is incremented if a valid echo request packet is received at a UDP EchoPlus server but for some reason cannot be responded to (e.g. due to local buffer overflow, CPU utilization, etc...). If PacketSuccess is false , TestRespReplyFailureCount SHOULD be 0.

commands.name: IPLayerCapacity()
commands.desc: [ASYNC] This command defines the IP Layer Capacity measurement configuration. IP Layer Capacity measurement is specified in [ TR-471 ]. Data received in the IP Layer Capacity measurement do not require storage on the device. If AuthenticationEnabled is set to true , one of the following combinations of AuthenticationCode , AuthenticationKeyID and AuthenticationKeyFileLocation MUST be met. Otherwise, the client returns an error. If only AuthenticationCode is provided, the client uses the value...

input.name: Interface
input.desc: The value MUST be the Path Name of a table row. The IP-layer interface over which the test is to be performed. Example: Device.IP.Interface.1 If the value is an empty string, the CPE MUST use its routing policy (IP Forwarding table entries), if necessary, to determine the appropriate interface.

input.name: Role
input.desc: [MANDATORY] Indicates whether the device will act as Sender or Receiver of test packets. Enumeration of: Receiver (The device will act as the Receiver) Sender (The device will act as the Sender)

input.name: ServerList
input.desc: [MANDATORY] Comma-separated list (up to 100 items) of strings (length up to 256, or ). A list of servers intended as testing partners for the client. The client works through the server list attempting individual test flows in a round-robin sequence. One flow is attempted to each server and all flows are required for testing, unless the optional FlowCount and MaximumFlows parameters are specified. The list contains each server’s Fully Qualified Domain Name or IP address and listening port in ...

input.name: JumboFramesPermitted
input.desc: If true , jumbo frames are allowed above 1 Gbps. The default value SHOULD be true .

input.name: MTU
input.desc: The MTU to be used for this test. Common MTU settings are 1500, 1250 and 9000. The default value MUST be 1500 .

input.name: LocalInterfaceRateIncluded
input.desc: When set to true , the client is invoked with the option which uses the bytes statistics on the interface along with the test traffic to determine the maximum IP layer capacity. When set to false , only test traffic is used to calculate IP layer capacity metrics. The default value MUST be true .

input.name: AuthenticationEnabled
input.desc: If true , client uses authentication for the test. If false , the client does not use authentication. Refer to Device.IP.Diagnostics.IPLayerCapacity() for description on how the input arguments are provided to enable authentication for the test. The default value MUST be false .

input.name: AuthenticationCode
input.desc: The authentication code or key to use when the client connects to the server. Refer to Device.IP.Diagnostics.IPLayerCapacity() for description on how the input arguments are provided to enable authentication for the test. When read, this parameter returns an empty string, regardless of the actual value, unless the Controller has a "secured" role.

input.name: AuthenticationKeyID
input.desc: The authentication key ID to use when the client connects to the server. Refer to Device.IP.Diagnostics.IPLayerCapacity() for description on how the input arguments are provided to enable authentication for the test.

input.name: AuthenticationKeyFileLocation
input.desc: The key file location the client uses to derive the key and key ID to be used for authentication. Refer to Device.IP.Diagnostics.IPLayerCapacity() for description on how the input arguments are provided to enable authentication for the test.

input.name: FlowCount
input.desc: Optional Number of flows required for a test. The default SHOULD be 0 (a magic number that indicates the parameter is not used). FlowCount MUST NOT be set to a value greater than IPLayerMaxConnections .

input.name: MaximumFlows
input.desc: Optional number of flows to attempt. MaximumFlows must be greater than the size of ServerList or FlowCount. The default SHOULD be 0 (a magic number that indicates the parameter is not used). MaximumFlows MUST NOT be set to a value greater than IPLayerMaxConnections .

input.name: EthernetPriority
input.desc: Ethernet priority code for marking packets transmitted in the test (if applicable). The default value SHOULD be zero.

input.name: DSCP
input.desc: The DiffServ code point for marking packets transmitted in the test. The default value SHOULD be zero.

input.name: ProtocolVersion
input.desc: Indicates the IP protocol version to be used. The default value SHOULD be Any . Enumeration of: Any (Use either IPv4 or IPv6 depending on the system preference) IPv4 (Use IPv4 for the requests) IPv6 (Use IPv6 for the requests)

input.name: UDPPayloadMin
input.desc: Minimum reference size of UDP payload in octets . No default. The implementation will algorithmically determine a value if none is configured. The value SHOULD be set to a value that avoids fragmentation (i.e., using path MTU discovery).

input.name: UDPPayloadMax
input.desc: Maximum reference size of UDP payload in octets . No default. The implementation will algorithmically determine a value if none is configured. The value SHOULD be set to the largest value that avoids fragmentation (i.e., using path MTU discovery). If JumboFramesPermitted is false , the maximum value MUST be 1472 octets. If JumboFramesPermitted is true , this value can be as large as 8972 octets. UDPPayloadMax MUST be greater than or equal to UDPPayloadMin .

input.name: UDPPayloadContent
input.desc: UDP Payload Content Type, If there is payload compression in the path and tests intend to characterize a possible advantage due to compression, then payload content SHOULD be supplied by a pseudo-random sequence generator, by using part of a compressed file, or by other means. Payload may also contain the test protocol PDUs. The default value SHOULD be zeroes . Enumeration of: zeroes (All zero (0) payload content) ones (All one (1) payload content) alternates0and1 (Alternating zero (0) and on...

input.name: PortMin
input.desc: Starting value for range of Dynamic Ports supported for test traffic and status feedback messages. PortMin MUST be less than or equal to PortMax , if specified. If PortMin and PortMax are not specified, the full range of Ports in the Dynamic Ports range (49152-65535) that have been specifically set aside by IANA MAY be used.

input.name: PortMax
input.desc: Indicates the upper bound of the supported Dynamic Port range, where PortMin indicates the starting port number. PortMax MUST be greater than or equal to PortMin , if specified. If PortMin and PortMax are not specified, the full range of Ports in the Dynamic Ports range (49152-65535) that have been specifically set aside by IANA MAY be used.

input.name: PortOptionalMin
input.desc: Starting value for range of User Ports supported for test traffic and status feedback messages. A value of zero (0) indicates no User Ports are used for test traffic or status feedback messages.

input.name: PortOptionalMax
input.desc: Indicates the upper bound of the supported User Port range, where PortOptionalMin indicates the starting port number. PortOptionalMax MUST be greater than or equal to PortOptionalMin . A value of zero (0) indicates no User Ports are used for test traffic or status feedback messages.

input.name: TestType
input.desc: Indicates the type of IP-Layer Capacity test being run. The default value SHOULD be Search . Enumeration of: Search (Search algorithm will be used to determine sending rate) Fixed (Fixed sending rate will be used)

input.name: IPDVEnable
input.desc: Enables one-way IPDV (IP Packet Delay Variation) metric for load rate adjustment algorithm. When true (enabled), one-way delay variation is used, otherwise round-trip delay variation is used. The default value SHOULD be false .

input.name: IPRREnable
input.desc: Enables IPRR (IP packet Reordering Ratio) metric. The default value SHOULD be false .

input.name: RIPREnable
input.desc: Enables RIPRR (Replicated IP Packet Ratio) metric. The default value SHOULD be false .

input.name: PreambleDuration
input.desc: Duration of the preamble testing, when traffic is being sent and/or received but the test clock has not been started. This is done to ensure all network elements in the path are "awake". The default value SHOULD be 2 seconds . Value specified in seconds .

input.name: MaximumTestBandwidth
input.desc: The rate limiting or admission control bandwidth to be configured on the client for the test. A value of 0 indicates the client does not use rate limiting or admission control. The value is expressed in Mbps . The default value MUST be 0 .

input.name: StartSendingRate
input.desc: The Sending Rate for a Fixed test or the initial Sending Rate value for a Search test. Value specified in kbps . The default value SHOULD be 500 kbps .

input.name: StartSendingRateIndex
input.desc: The configurable initial Sending Rate index (to a row of the sending rate table) for a Fixed or Search test. StartSendingRateIndex overrides StartSendingRate if both parameters are present. See Annex A of [ TR-471 ] for details. The default value SHOULD be 0.

input.name: NumberTestSubIntervals
input.desc: Number of intermediate measurement reporting intervals. The value MUST NOT be greater than IPLayerMaxIncrementalResult . The default value SHOULD be 10.

input.name: NumberFirstModeTestSubIntervals
input.desc: When the value >= 1, bimodal test mode is requested and the value represents the number of sub-intervals to be included in the first capacity test mode. The remaining sub-intervals of NumberTestSubIntervals are for the second capacity test mode. Value = 0 indicates that bimodal testing is disabled. The value MUST NOT be greater than NumberTestSubIntervals . The default value SHOULD be 0.

input.name: TestSubInterval
input.desc: Duration of intermediate measurement reporting intervals. TestSubInterval * NumberTestSubIntervals MUST result in an integer value in seconds, in the range 5 seconds <= TestSubInterval * NumberTestSubIntervals <= 60 seconds. The default value SHOULD be 1000 milliseconds . Value specified in milliseconds .

input.name: StatusFeedbackInterval
input.desc: Period of status feedback message (receiver of offered load returns messages to the sender with results of measured metrics). Value specified in milliseconds . The default value SHOULD be 50 milliseconds .

input.name: TimeoutNoTestTraffic
input.desc: Timeout value. If no test traffic packets are received for TimeoutNoTestTraffic milliseconds , test will timeout. Value specified in milliseconds . The default value SHOULD be 1000 milliseconds .

input.name: TimeoutNoStatusMessage
input.desc: Timeout value. If no status message packets are received for TimeoutNoStatusMessage milliseconds , test will timeout. Value specified in milliseconds . The default value SHOULD be 1000 milliseconds .

input.name: Tmax
input.desc: Maximum waiting time for packets to arrive. Value specified in milliseconds . The default value SHOULD be 1000 milliseconds .

input.name: TmaxRTT
input.desc: Maximum Round Trip Time waiting time for packets to arrive. Value specified in milliseconds . The default value SHOULD be 3000 milliseconds .

input.name: TimestampResolution
input.desc: Indicates the requested precision of timestamp values. The test implementation will determine the actual precision to use based on the implemented resolution capabilities of the protocols used and this requested value. If the implemented resolution capabilities of the IPLayerCapSupportedMetrics protocols being used are able to provide the requested resolution, this resolution SHOULD be provided. Value specified in microseconds . The default value SHOULD be 1 microseconds .

input.name: SeqErrThresh
input.desc: This parameter is only meaningful if TestType is Search . Threshold for Loss or Reordering or Replication impairments measured (events where received packet sequence number did not increase by one). The default value SHOULD be 10.

input.name: ReordDupIgnoreEnable
input.desc: This parameter is only meaningful if TestType is Search . When true (enabled) only Loss counts toward received packet sequence number errors, and Reordering and Duplication impairments are ignored. When false (disabled), Loss, Reordering and Duplication are all counted as sequence number errors. The default value SHOULD be true (enabled).

input.name: LowerThresh
input.desc: This parameter is only meaningful if TestType is Search . The lower threshold on the range of Round Trip Time (RTT) variation. Value specified in milliseconds . The default value SHOULD be 30 milliseconds .

input.name: UpperThresh
input.desc: This parameter is only meaningful if TestType is Search . The upper threshold on the range of Round Trip Time (RTT) variation. Value specified in milliseconds . The default value SHOULD be 90 milliseconds .

input.name: RetryThresh
input.desc: The initial number of retries before activating “fast” sending rate increase mode. Different paths through the flow chart increase the sending rate, either fast or slow, or decrease the rate, etc. The algorithm doubles the threshold each time on subsequent activations. See Annex B of [ TR-471 ] for details. The default value SHOULD be 5.

input.name: HighSpeedDelta
input.desc: This parameter is only meaningful if TestType is Search . The number of rows to move in a single adjustment when initially increasing offered load (to ramp up quickly). The default value SHOULD be 10.

input.name: RateAdjAlgorithm
input.desc: Configurable choice of Load Rate Adjustment Algorithm. Refer to [ TR-471 ] for details. Enumeration of: B (Use type "B" Load Rate Adjustment Algorithm. See section 5.2.1 in [ TR-471 ] for details) C (Use type "C" Load Rate Adjustment Algorithm. See Annex B in [ TR-471 ] for details)

input.name: SlowAdjThresh
input.desc: This parameter is only meaningful if TestType is Search . Threshold on the measured number of consecutive status reports indicating loss and/or delay variation above UpperThresh (SlowAdjCount). The default value SHOULD be 3.

input.name: HSpeedThresh
input.desc: This parameter is only meaningful if TestType is Search . Threshold for transition between low and high sending rate step sizes (such as 1Mbps and 100 Mbps). If JumboFramesPermitted is true this may result in use of jumbo frames. The default value SHOULD be 1 Gbps .

output.name: ⇐ Status
output.desc: Indicates the availability of diagnostics data. Enumeration of: Complete Error_CannotResolveHostName Error_NoRouteToHost Error_InitConnectionFailed Error_NoResponse Error_PasswordRequestFailed Error_LoginFailed Error_RejectedByRemote Error_IncorrectSize Error_Timeout Error_Internal Error_Other If the value of this parameter is anything other than Complete , the values of the other results parameters for this test are indeterminate.

output.name: ⇐ StatusCode
output.desc: Status code of the test returned by the client, if applicable.

output.name: ⇐ StatusMessage
output.desc: Status message of the test returned by the client, if applicable.

output.name: ⇐ BOMTime
output.desc: Beginning of transmission send/receive time in UTC, which MUST be specified to TimestampResolution precision. If multiple connections are used, then BOMTime is set to the earliest value across all connections. For example: 2008-04-09T15:01:05.123456Z

output.name: ⇐ EOMTime
output.desc: End of transmission in UTC, which MUST be specified to TimestampResolution precision. If multiple connections are used, then EOMTime is set to the latest value across all connections. For example: 2008-04-09T15:01:05.123456Z

output.name: ⇐ TmaxUsed
output.desc: Configured value of Tmax used in the test. This value is expressed in milliseconds .

output.name: ⇐ TestInterval
output.desc: Duration of the test (either downlink or uplink). This value is expected to equal TestSubInterval * NumberTestSubIntervals . This value is expressed in seconds .

output.name: ⇐ MaxIPLayerCapacity
output.desc: The maximum IP-Layer Capacity metric from among all IncrementalResult.{i}.IPLayerCapacity values measured between BOMTime and EOMTime across all connections for this test. This is calculated according to [ TR-471 ] Equation 1. Result is expressed in Mbps with 2 digits beyond the decimal. 10 6 bits/second = 1 Mbps .

output.name: ⇐ TimeOfMax
output.desc: Time in UTC of end of the sub-interval when MaxIPLayerCapacity was measured. If the value of MaxIPLayerCapacity occurred in multiple sub-intervals, this MUST be the earliest of these sub-intervals. Value MUST be specified to TimestampResolution precision. For example: 2008-04-09T15:01:05.123456Z

output.name: ⇐ MaxETHCapacityNoFCS
output.desc: Results of measurements using the Maximum IP-Layer Capacity metric, according to [ TR-471 ] Equation 1, and calculations to estimate the capacity at Layer 2 with Preamble and Inter-frame gap, but no ETH Frame Check Sequence. Result is expressed in Mbps with 2 digits beyond the decimal. 10 6 bits/second = 1 Mbps .

output.name: ⇐ MaxETHCapacityWithFCS
output.desc: Results of measurements using the Maximum IP-Layer Capacity metric, according to [ TR-471 ] Equation 1, and calculations to estimate the capacity at Layer 2 with ETH Frame Check Sequence. Result is expressed in Mbps with 2 digits beyond the decimal. 10 6 bits/second = 1 Mbps .

output.name: ⇐ MaxETHCapacityWithFCSVLAN
output.desc: Results of measurements using the Maximum IP-Layer Capacity metric, according to [ TR-471 ] Equation 1, and calculations to estimate the capacity at Layer 2 with ETH Frame Check Sequence and VLAN tag. Result is expressed in Mbps with 2 digits beyond the decimal. 10 6 bits/second = 1 Mbps .

output.name: ⇐ LossRatioAtMax
output.desc: Ratio of lost packets to total packets during sub-interval of MaxIPLayerCapacity . This value is expressed as a decimal to 9 decimal digits.

output.name: ⇐ RTTRangeAtMax
output.desc: The range of Round Trip Time (RTT) during sub-interval of MaxIPLayerCapacity . This value is expressed in seconds . This value is expressed as a decimal to 9 decimal digits.

output.name: ⇐ PDVRangeAtMax
output.desc: The range of Packet Delay Variation (PDV) during sub-interval of MaxIPLayerCapacity . This value is expressed in seconds . This value is expressed as a decimal to 9 decimal digits.

output.name: ⇐ MinOnewayDelayAtMax
output.desc: The minimum one-way delay during the sub-interval of MaxIPLayerCapacity . The minimum one-way delay is calculated at the conclusion of the test and SHALL be calculated using the conditional distribution of all packets with a finite one-way delay value (undefined delays are excluded). This value is expressed in seconds . This value is expressed as a decimal to 9 decimal digits.

output.name: ⇐ ReorderedRatioAtMax
output.desc: Ratio of reordered packets to total packets during the sub-interval of MaxIPLayerCapacity . This value is expressed as a decimal to 9 decimal digits.

output.name: ⇐ ReplicatedRatioAtMax
output.desc: Ratio of replicated packets to total packets during the sub-interval of MaxIPLayerCapacity . This value is expressed as a decimal to 9 decimal digits.

output.name: ⇐ RTTMinAtMax
output.desc: The value of minimum Round Trip Time (RTT) during the sub interval of MaxIPLayerCapacity . This value is expressed as a decimal to 9 decimal digits.

output.name: ⇐ RTTMaxAtMax
output.desc: The value of maximum Round Trip Time (RTT) during the sub interval of MaxIPLayerCapacity . This value is expressed as a decimal to 9 decimal digits.

output.name: ⇐ InterfaceEthMbpsAtMax
output.desc: The number of bits observed on the Interface during an IP-Layer Capacity test for time interval of duration TestSubInterval ending at IncrementalResult.{i}.TimeOfSubInterval corresponding to the MaxIPLayerCapacity , divided by the duration of TestSubInterval . Result is expressed in Mbps with 2 digits beyond the decimal. 10 6 bits/second = 1 Mbps . This is primarily a diagnostic measurement. Measurement direction follows the Role .

output.name: ⇐ IPLayerCapacitySummary
output.desc: The IP-Layer Capacity metric from among all IncrementalResult.{i}.IPLayerCapacity values measured between BOMTime and EOMTime across all connections for this test. This is calculated according to [ TR-471 ] Equation 1. Result is expressed in Mbps with 2 digits beyond the decimal. 10 6 bits/second = 1 Mbps .

output.name: ⇐ LossRatioSummary
output.desc: Ratio of lost packets to total packets during the complete TestInterval . This value is expressed as a decimal to 9 decimal digits.

output.name: ⇐ RTTRangeSummary
output.desc: The range of measured Round Trip Time (RTT) during the complete TestInterval . This value is expressed in seconds , as a decimal to 9 decimal digits.

output.name: ⇐ PDVRangeSummary
output.desc: The range of Packet Delay Variation (PDV) during the complete TestInterval . This value is expressed in seconds , as a decimal to 9 decimal digits.

output.name: ⇐ MinOnewayDelaySummary
output.desc: The minimum one-way delay during the complete TestInterval . This value is expressed in seconds , as a decimal to 9 decimal digits.

output.name: ⇐ MinRTTSummary
output.desc: The minimum RTT during the complete TestInterval . This value is expressed in seconds , as a decimal to 9 decimal digits.

output.name: ⇐ ReorderedRatioSummary
output.desc: Ratio of reordered packets to total packets during the complete TestInterval . This value is expressed as a decimal to 9 decimal digits.

output.name: ⇐ ReplicatedRatioSummary
output.desc: Ratio of replicated packets to total packets during the complete TestInterval . This value is expressed as a decimal to 9 decimal digits.

output.name: ⇐ InterfaceEthMbpsSummary
output.desc: The number of bits observed on the Interface during an IP-Layer Capacity test for the entire time interval of duration TestInterval , divided by the duration of TestInterval . Result is expressed in Mbps with 2 digits beyond the decimal. 10 6 bits/second = 1 Mbps . This is primarily a diagnostic measurement. Measurement direction follows the Role .

output.name: ⇐ TmaxRTTUsed
output.desc: Configured value of TmaxRTT used in the test. This value is expressed in milliseconds .

output.name: ⇐ TimestampResolutionUsed
output.desc: Indicates the timestamp resolution of reported results. This is a function of the measurement protocol, and it is usually determined once the protocol chosen. Value specified in microseconds .

output.name: ⇐ ActiveFlows
output.desc: Number of flows set-up and used for a test.

output.name: ⇐ ModalResult.{i}.
output.desc: Modal test results. Only returned when bimodal test mode is enabled ( NumberFirstModeTestSubIntervals >=1). If returned, it MUST contain 1 or more entries, with instance number 1 corresponding to the second mode and instance number 2 corresponding to the third mode. Results for the Maximum in each mode/instance are calculated based on IncrementalResult.{i}. data within the boundary of its corresponding mode. This table MUST contain at least 1 entry. This table's Instance Numbers MUST be 1, 2,...

output.name: ⇐ MaxIPLayerCapacity
output.desc: The maximum IP-Layer Capacity metric from among all IncrementalResult.{i}.IPLayerCapacity values within corresponding mode across all connections for this test. This is calculated according to [ TR-471 ] Equation 1. Result is expressed in Mbps with 2 digits beyond the decimal. 10 6 bits/second = 1 Mbps .

output.name: ⇐ TimeOfMax
output.desc: Time in UTC of end of the sub-interval when MaxIPLayerCapacity was measured. If the value of MaxIPLayerCapacity occurred in multiple sub-intervals, this MUST be the earliest of these sub-intervals. Value MUST be specified to TimestampResolution precision. For example: 2008-04-09T15:01:05.123456Z

output.name: ⇐ MaxETHCapacityNoFCS
output.desc: Results of measurements using the Maximum IP-Layer Capacity metric, according to [ TR-471 ] Equation 1, and calculations to estimate the capacity at Layer 2 with Preamble and Inter-frame gap, but no ETH Frame Check Sequence. Result is expressed in Mbps with 2 digits beyond the decimal. 10 6 bits/second = 1 Mbps .

output.name: ⇐ MaxETHCapacityWithFCS
output.desc: Results of measurements using the Maximum IP-Layer Capacity metric, according to [ TR-471 ] Equation 1, and calculations to estimate the capacity at Layer 2 with ETH Frame Check Sequence. Result is expressed in Mbps with 2 digits beyond the decimal. 10 6 bits/second = 1 Mbps .

output.name: ⇐ MaxETHCapacityWithFCSVLAN
output.desc: Results of measurements using the Maximum IP-Layer Capacity metric, according to [ TR-471 ] Equation 1, and calculations to estimate the capacity at Layer 2 with ETH Frame Check Sequence and VLAN tag. Result is expressed in Mbps with 2 digits beyond the decimal. 10 6 bits/second = 1 Mbps .

output.name: ⇐ LossRatioAtMax
output.desc: Ratio of lost packets to total packets during sub-interval of MaxIPLayerCapacity . This value is expressed as a decimal to 9 decimal digits.

output.name: ⇐ RTTRangeAtMax
output.desc: The range of Round Trip Time (RTT) during sub-interval of MaxIPLayerCapacity . This value is expressed in seconds . This value is expressed as a decimal to 9 decimal digits.

output.name: ⇐ PDVRangeAtMax
output.desc: The range of Packet Delay Variation (PDV) during sub-interval of MaxIPLayerCapacity . This value is expressed in seconds . This value is expressed as a decimal to 9 decimal digits.

output.name: ⇐ MinOnewayDelayAtMax
output.desc: The minimum one-way delay during the sub-interval of MaxIPLayerCapacity . The minimum one-way delay is calculated at the conclusion of the test and SHALL be calculated using the conditional distribution of all packets with a finite one-way delay value (undefined delays are excluded). This value is expressed in seconds . This value is expressed as a decimal to 9 decimal digits.

output.name: ⇐ ReorderedRatioAtMax
output.desc: Ratio of reordered packets to total packets during the sub-interval of MaxIPLayerCapacity . This value is expressed as a decimal to 9 decimal digits.

output.name: ⇐ ReplicatedRatioAtMax
output.desc: Ratio of replicated packets to total packets during the sub-interval of MaxIPLayerCapacity . This value is expressed as a decimal to 9 decimal digits.

output.name: ⇐ InterfaceEthMbpsAtMax
output.desc: The number of bits observed on the Interface during an IP-Layer Capacity test for time interval of duration TestSubInterval ending at IncrementalResult.{i}.TimeOfSubInterval corresponding to the MaxIPLayerCapacity , divided by the duration of TestSubInterval . Result is expressed in Mbps with 2 digits beyond the decimal. 10 6 bits/second = 1 Mbps . This is primarily a diagnostic measurement. Measurement direction follows the Role .

output.name: ⇐ IncrementalResult.{i}.
output.desc: Results for time segmented tests (tests where NumberTestSubIntervals > 1). This data is calculated across all connections in the test. A new object is created every TestSubInterval after that interval has completed. Instance numbers MUST start at 1 and sequentially increment as new instances are created. All instances are removed when new test is started or results are otherwise cleared. This table's Instance Numbers MUST be 1, 2, 3... (assigned sequentially without gaps).

output.name: ⇐ IPLayerCapacity
output.desc: Results of measurements using the maximum IP-Layer Capacity metric calculation for a single interval from [ TR-471 ] Equation 1, for time interval of duration IPLayerCapacity().Input.TestSubInterval ending at TimeOfSubInterval across all connections for this test. Result is expressed in Mbps with 2 digits beyond the decimal. 10 6 bits/second = 1 Mbps .

output.name: ⇐ TimeOfSubInterval
output.desc: Time in UTC of end of sub-interval when IPLayerCapacity was measured. Value MUST be specified to IPLayerCapacity().Input.TimestampResolution precision. For example: 2008-04-09T15:01:05.123456Z

output.name: ⇐ LossRatio
output.desc: Ratio of lost packets to total packets, for time interval of duration IPLayerCapacity().Input.TestSubInterval ending at TimeOfSubInterval across all connections for this test. This value is expressed as a decimal to 9 decimal digits.

output.name: ⇐ RTTRange
output.desc: The range of Round Trip Time (RTT), for time interval of duration IPLayerCapacity().Input.TestSubInterval ending at TimeOfSubInterval across all connections for this test. See [ TR-471 ] for description of how value is calculated. This value is expressed in seconds . This value is expressed as a decimal to 9 decimal digits.

output.name: ⇐ PDVRange
output.desc: The range of Packet Delay Variation (PDV), for time interval of duration IPLayerCapacity().Input.TestSubInterval ending at TimeOfSubInterval across all connections for this test. See [ TR-471 ] for description of how value is calculated. This value is expressed in seconds . This value is expressed as a decimal to 9 decimal digits.

output.name: ⇐ MinOnewayDelay
output.desc: The minimum one-way delay, for time interval of duration IPLayerCapacity().Input.TestSubInterval ending at TimeOfSubInterval across all connections for this test. The minimum one-way delay is calculated at the conclusion of the test and SHALL be calculated using the conditional distribution of all packets with a finite one-way delay value (undefined delays are excluded). This value is expressed in seconds . This value is expressed as a decimal to 9 decimal digits.

output.name: ⇐ ReorderedRatio
output.desc: Ratio of reordered packets to total packets, for time interval of duration IPLayerCapacity().Input.TestSubInterval ending at TimeOfSubInterval across all connections for this test. This value is expressed as a decimal to 9 decimal digits.

output.name: ⇐ ReplicatedRatio
output.desc: Ratio of replicated packets to total packets, for time interval of duration IPLayerCapacity().Input.TestSubInterval ending at TimeOfSubInterval across all connections for this test. This value is expressed as a decimal to 9 decimal digits.

output.name: ⇐ InterfaceEthMbps
output.desc: The number of bits observed on the IPLayerCapacity().Input.Interface during an IP-Layer Capacity test for time interval of duration IPLayerCapacity().Input.TestSubInterval ending at TimeOfSubInterval , divided by the duration of IPLayerCapacity().Input.TestSubInterval . Result is expressed in Mbps with 2 digits beyond the decimal. 10 6 bits/second = 1 Mbps . This is primarily a diagnostic measurement. Measurement direction follows the IPLayerCapacity().Input.Role .

commands.name: ServerSelectionDiagnostics()
commands.desc: [ASYNC] This command provides access to a diagnostics test that performs either an ICMP Ping or UDP Echo ping against multiple hosts determining which one has the smallest average response time. There MUST be a ping response to the transmitted ping, or timeout, before the next ping is sent out.

input.name: Interface
input.desc: The value MUST be the Path Name of the IP-layer interface over which the test is to be performed. Example: Device.IP.Interface.1 If the value is an empty string, the CPE MUST use its routing policy (IP Forwarding table entries), if necessary, to determine the appropriate interface.

input.name: ProtocolVersion
input.desc: [MANDATORY] Indicates the IP protocol version to be used. Enumeration of: Any (Use either IPv4 or IPv6 depending on the system preference) IPv4 (Use IPv4 for the requests) IPv6 (Use IPv6 for the requests) The default value MUST be Any .

input.name: Protocol
input.desc: [MANDATORY] The protocol over which the test is to be performed. Enumeration of: ICMP UDP Echo

input.name: HostList
input.desc: [MANDATORY] Comma-separated list (up to 10 items) (length ) of strings (maximum number of characters per item 256). Each entry is a Host name or address of a host to ping.

input.name: NumberOfRepetitions
input.desc: [MANDATORY] Number of repetitions of the ping test to perform for each HostList entry before reporting the results.

input.name: Timeout
input.desc: [MANDATORY] Timeout in milliseconds for each iteration of the ping test where the total number of iterations is the value of NumberOfRepetitions times the number of entities in the HostList Parameter.

output.name: ⇐ Status
output.desc: Indicates the availability of diagnostics data. Enumeration of: Complete Error_CannotResolveHostName Error_Internal Error_Other If the value of this parameter is anything other than Complete , the values of the other results parameters for this test are indeterminate.

output.name: ⇐ FastestHost
output.desc: Result parameter indicating the Host (one of the items within the HostList Parameter) with the smallest average response time.

output.name: ⇐ MinimumResponseTime
output.desc: Result parameter indicating the minimum response time in microseconds over all repetitions with successful responses of the most recent ping test for the Host identified in FastestHost . Success is defined by the underlying protocol used. If there were no successful responses across all Hosts, this value MUST be zero.

output.name: ⇐ AverageResponseTime
output.desc: Result parameter indicating the average response time in microseconds over all repetitions with successful responses of the most recent ping test for the Host identified in FastestHost . Success is defined by the underlying protocol used. If there were no successful responses across all Hosts, this value MUST be zero.

output.name: ⇐ MaximumResponseTime
output.desc: Result parameter indicating the maximum response time in microseconds over all repetitions with successful responses of the most recent ping test for the Host identified in FastestHost . Success is defined by the underlying protocol used. If there were no successful responses across all Hosts, this value MUST be zero.

output.name: ⇐ IPAddressUsed
output.desc: [ IPAddress ] Indicates which IP address was used to send the request to the host identified in FastestHost .

commands.desc: Reset all this object's statistics counters to zero.

commands.name: StatsReset()
commands.desc: This command represents a request to reset all statistics counters to zero. Statistics are provided in InterfaceSetting.{i}.Stats. .

commands.name: MACTest()
commands.desc: This command allows the MAC key and MAC algorithm to be tested to see if they produce an expected outcome. The command calculates a MAC for InputString using the KeyValue and MACKeyAlgorithm and compares that to the value of InputMAC . If the values match, the output Match is true .

input.name: InputString
input.desc: [MANDATORY] The command calculates a MAC of InputString using the KeyValue and MACKeyAlgorithm .

input.name: InputMAC
input.desc: [MANDATORY] The command compares the calculated MAC to InputMAC .

output.name: ⇐ Match
output.desc: Match is true if the calculated MAC and InputMAC are the same.

commands.name: RemoveInactiveHosts()
commands.desc: Removes Host entries where Host.{i}.Active is false , and the Host has been inactive for longer than MinimumInactiveTime . The inactivity duration is calculated based on the Host.{i}.ActiveLastChange timestamp.

input.name: MinimumInactiveTime
input.desc: Specifies the minimum duration, in seconds , for which a Host must be inactive before being removed. When MinimumInactiveTime is not specified, all inactive Host entries are removed.

output.name: ⇐ NumberOfRemovedHosts
output.desc: Indicates the total number of hosts successfully removed.

commands.name: FlushCache()
commands.desc: This command empties the cache.

commands.name: Reset()
commands.desc: Reset all this object's statistics counters to zero.

commands.name: NSLookupDiagnostics()
commands.desc: [ASYNC] This command defines access to an IP-layer NS Lookup test for the specified IP interface. When initiated, the NS Lookup test will contact DNSServer and look up HostName NumberOfRepetitions times. There will be a Result instance for each time the device performs a DNS lookup, which is determined by the value of NumberOfRepetitions . Any previous Result instances are removed when a new test is initiated.

input.name: Interface
input.desc: The value MUST be the Path Name of a table row. The layer 3 interface over which the test is to be performed. Example: Device.IP.Interface.1 . If the value is an empty string, the CPE MUST use its routing policy (IP Forwarding table entries), if necessary, to determine the appropriate interface.

input.name: HostName
input.desc: [MANDATORY] Specifies the Host Name that NS Lookup is to look for. The current domain name MUST be used unless the name is a fully qualified name.

input.name: DNSServer
input.desc: Specifies the DNS Server name or IP address that NS Lookup is to use for the lookup. The name of this server will be resolved using the default DNS server unless an IP address is provided. If an empty string is specified, the device's default DNS server will be used.

input.name: Timeout

output.desc: true if the firmware was updated as a result of the boot that caused this Event Notification; otherwise false .

output.name: ParameterMap
output.desc: Boot parameters configured via the recipient Controller's LocalAgent.Controller.{i}.BootParameter table. Formatted as a [ JSONObject ] A JSON Object as defined in [ Section 4/RFC7159 ].

events.name: MemoryCriticalState!
events.desc: This event is generated indicating critical condition is reached i.e., when MemUtilization exceeds the rise threshold, the event is generated.

output.name: MemUtilization
output.desc: Memory utilization, in percent , rounded to the nearest whole percent , collected at the polling interval.

events.name: CPUCriticalState!
events.desc: This event is generated indicating critical condition is reached i.e., when the rise threshold is crossed, the event is generated.

output.name: CPUUtilization
output.desc: CPU utilization, in percent , rounded to the nearest whole percent .

output.name: Name
output.desc: Name of this CPU. This text MUST be sufficient to distinguish this CPU from other CPUs.

events.name: HighTemperatureAlarm!
events.desc: This event is triggered when the temperature sensor detects a high temperature. If the Enable parameter is true , the event is triggered exactly once when the Value value rises above HighAlarmValue .

output.name: Value
output.desc: The current temperature value that triggered the event. This value is in degrees celsius .

events.name: LowTemperatureAlarm!
events.desc: This event is triggered when the temperature sensor detects a low temperature. If the Enable parameter is true , the event is triggered exactly once when the Value value falls below LowAlarmValue .

output.name: Value
output.desc: The current temperature value that triggered the event. This value is in degrees celsius .

events.name: BelowPhyThresholdTrap!
events.desc: If transmit PHY rate between all pairs of MoCA Nodes are greater than or equal to PhyThreshold , and subsequently the transmit PHY rate of one pair of MoCA Nodes drops below PhyThreshold , send this notification if PhyThresholdTrapEnable is true . This trap comes from the [ MOCA20-MIB ] and is provided for debug purposes.

output.name: LowestPhyRate
output.desc: The lowest PHY rate in the MoCA network, of Mesh.{i}.TxRate , which is the transmit PHY rate from the MoCA Node specified with Mesh.{i}.TxNodeIndex , to the MoCA Node specified with Mesh.{i}.RxNodeIndex . If multiple links have the same lowest PHY rate, sends the PHY rate for the link with the lowest Mesh.{i}.TxNodeIndex . If multiple links with the same Mesh.{i}.TxNodeIndex have the same lowest PHY rate, sends the PHY rate for the link with the lowest Mesh.{i}.RxNodeIndex . Network managemen...

events.name: AbovePhyThresholdTrap!
events.desc: If transmit PHY rate between one or more pairs of MoCA Nodes are less than PhyThreshold , and subsequently the transmit PHY rate between all pairs of MoCA Nodes goes above or is equal to PhyThreshold , send this notification if PhyThresholdTrapEnable is true . This trap comes from the [ MOCA20-MIB ] and is provided for debug purposes.

events.name: StatusChangeTrap!
events.desc: This trap is sent when StatusChangeEnable is true and Status changes value. This trap comes from the [ MOCA20-MIB ] and is provided for debug purposes.

output.name: Status
output.desc: The current value of Status .

events.name: NumNodesChangeTrap!
events.desc: This trap is sent when NumNodesChangeEnable is true and NumNodes changes value. This trap comes from the [ MOCA20-MIB ] and is provided for debug purposes.

output.name: NumNodes
output.desc: The current value of NumNodes .

events.name: MrRstSuccessTrap!
events.desc: An MR Entry Node reports that the network got reset successfully (MRRST_SUCCESS Event). This trap comes from the [ MOCA20-MIB ] and is provided for debug purposes.

events.name: MrRstFailTrap!
events.desc: An MR Entry Node reports that the network reset did not complete successfully (MRRST_FAIL Event). This trap comes from the [ MOCA20-MIB ] and is provided for debug purposes.

events.name: MrNetworkSuccessTrap!
events.desc: An MR Entry Node reports that the network got reformed successfully following the MR transaction (MRNETWORK_SUCCESS Event). This trap comes from the [ MOCA20-MIB ] and is provided for debug purposes.

events.name: MrNetworkFailTrap!
events.desc: An MR Entry Node reports that the MR transaction failed, and the network did not get reformed (MRNETWORK_FAIL Event). This trap comes from the [ MOCA20-MIB ] and is provided for debug purposes.

events.name: PowerStateBcstRecTrap!
events.desc: When the MoCA Node is in Power State M1 or M2, indicates that the MoCA Node has received a Broadcast data MSDU, which is available at the data interface (POWER_STATEBCST_REC Event). This trap comes from the [ MOCA20-MIB ] and is provided for debug purposes.

events.name: PowerStateM0NcTrap!
events.desc: When a MoCA Node is in Power State M1, indicates that it is going to move to Power State M0 due to the NCs instruction. This trap comes from the [ MOCA20-MIB ] and is provided for debug purposes.

events.name: PowerStateNc1xTrap!
events.desc: When the MoCA Node is in Power State M1/M2/M3, indicates that MoCA 1 Node is the NC (POWER_STATENC_1X Event). This trap comes from the [ MOCA20-MIB ] and is provided for debug purposes.

events.name: PowerStateNetVerTrap!
events.desc: When the MoCA Node is in Power State M2 or M3, indicates that the network MoCA version is changed (POWER_STATENET_VER Event). This trap comes from the [ MOCA20-MIB ] and is provided for debug purposes.

events.name: PowerStateRespTrap!
events.desc: Carries the response of the MoCA Node to a request (through POWER_STATEREQ) to transition into a desired Power State (POWER_STATERESP Event). This trap comes from the [ MOCA20-MIB ] and is provided for debug purposes.

events.name: PowerStateUcstPenTrap!
events.desc: When the MoCA Node is in Power State M2, indicates that a Unicast data MSDU destined to the MoCA Node is pending (POWER_STATEUCST_PEN Event). This trap comes from the [ MOCA20-MIB ] and is provided for debug purposes.

events.name: PowerStateTrnsReqTrap!
events.desc: When a MoCA Node is in Power State M1 or M2, requests to transition to Power State M0 (POWER_STATETRNS_REQ Event). This trap comes from the [ MOCA20-MIB ] and is provided for debug purposes.

events.name: PowerStateWupUrTrap!
events.desc: When the MoCA Node is in Power State M2, this reports a wakeup request from NC due to unspecified reasons (POWER_STATEWUP_UR Event). This trap comes from the [ MOCA20-MIB ] and is provided for debug purposes.

events.name: LmoStatusTrap!
events.desc: When LmoTrapEnable is enabled, reports that the MoCA Node is starting LMO (Link Maintenance Operation). This trap comes from the [ MOCA20-MIB ] and is provided for debug purposes.

events.name: LinkFailureTrap!
events.desc: Indicates a link failure. If the failure was an Admission or LMO failure, LinkState indicates when the link was dropped within the sequence. This trap comes from the [ MOCA20-MIB ] and is provided for debug purposes.

events.name: ConnectedNodesChangeTrap!
events.desc: This trap is sent when ConnectedNodesChangeTrapEn is true and ConnectedNodesInfo changes value. This trap comes from the MOCA25-MIB and is provided for debug purposes.

output.name: ConnectedNodesInfo
output.desc: The current value of ConnectedNodesInfo .

events.name: MgntEntityNetwIePayloadRecTrap!
events.desc: This trap is sent when MgntEntityNetwIePayloadRecTrapEn is true and MgntEntityNetIePayloadRx changes value. This trap comes from the MOCA25-MIB and is provided for debug purposes.

events.name: MpsInitScanRecTrap!
events.desc: This trap is sent when MpsTrapEn is true and MpsInitScanPayload changes value. This trap comes from the MOCA25-MIB and is provided for debug purposes.

output.name: MpsInitScanPayload
output.desc: The current value of MpsInitScanPayload .

events.name: MpsPairFailTrap!
events.desc: This trap is sent when MpsTrapEn is true , indicates a MPS pairing failure. This trap comes from the MOCA25-MIB and is provided for debug purposes.

events.name: MpsPrivacyChangedTrap!
events.desc: This trap is sent when MpsTrapEn is true , indicates that the Node's privacy settings (PRIVACYEN and/or PSWD) have been changed by MPS. This trap comes from the MOCA25-MIB and is provided for debug purposes.

events.name: NcPrivacySupportedRecTrap!
events.desc: This trap is sent when NcPrivSupportedRecTrapEn is true and PrivacyNc changes value. This trap comes from the MOCA25-MIB and is provided for debug purposes.

output.name: PrivacyNc
output.desc: The current value of PrivacyNc .

events.name: NetworkNameRecTrap!
events.desc: This trap is sent when NetworkNameRecTrapEn is true and NetworkNamePayload changes value. This trap comes from the MOCA25-MIB and is provided for debug purposes.

output.name: NetworkNamePayload
output.desc: The current value of NetworkNamePayload .

events.name: NodeDropAdmFailureTrap!
events.desc: This trap is sent when NodeDropTrapEn is true , indicates that the Node drops from the network due to admission failure. This trap comes from the MOCA25-MIB and is provided for debug purposes.

events.name: NodeDropNcTrap!
events.desc: This trap is sent when NodeDropTrapEn is true , indicates that the Node is dropped by the NC as indicated in the NODE_BITMASK and LOW_POWER_NODE_BITMASK. This trap comes from the MOCA25-MIB and is provided for debug purposes.

events.name: NodeDropMpsTriggeredTrap!
events.desc: This trap is sent when NodeDropTrapEn is true , indicates that MPS is locally triggered when the Node is un-Paired. This trap comes from the MOCA25-MIB and is provided for debug purposes.

events.name: NodeDropNcChgTrap!
events.desc: This trap is sent when NodeDropTrapEn is true , indicates that there is a NC change when the Node is Non-Secured Admitted Node. This trap comes from the MOCA25-MIB and is provided for debug purposes.

output.desc: [ MACAddress ] Unique identifier of the source BSS or AP_MLD_MAC_Addr for which the steering BTM report applies.

events.name: AgentOnboard!
events.desc: This reports an EasyMesh Agent Onboarding event [ Section 5/EasyMesh ].

output.name: DeviceID
output.desc: [ MACAddress ] A unique identifier for this onboarded device within the Wi-Fi network.

output.name: BackhaulSta
output.desc: [ MACAddress ] The MAC address of the interface on this onboarded device providing backhaul to this device.

output.name: BackhaulMACAddress
output.desc: [ MACAddress ] The MAC address of the interface on the network that is providing the backhaul for this EasyMesh Agent. For Wi-Fi backhaul, this is the BSSID or AP MLD address of the backhaul BSS.

output.name: BackhaulALID
output.desc: [ MACAddress ] The IEEE 1905 [ IEEE1905.1a ] Abstraction-Layer ID (ALID) of the EasyMesh Agent on the network that is providing the backhaul for this EasyMesh Agent.

events.name: BackhaulChange!
events.desc: Event containing the response to a Backhaul Steering Request. [ EasyMesh ]

output.desc: [ MACAddress ] The BSSID of the target BSS or the AP Multi-Link Device (MLD) MAC Address [ Section 17.2.33, Backhaul steering response TLV/EasyMesh ].
